commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Preserve embedding size overrides
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix rejection of valid dimensions=2048 requests for voyageai/voyage-4-nano by honoring its configured embedding size.

## Changes

- Honor hf_config.embedding_size before falling back to embedding_dim, Dense module output size, or hidden size.
- Preserve existing EmbeddingGemma 2 dimension support.

## Validation

43 tests passed, including the Voyage GPU regression on H800, pooling parameter tests, and EmbeddingGemma 2 configuration tests.

Before the fix, the Voyage regression failed because the dimension limit was incorrectly set to 1024. After the fix, dimensions=2048 returns 2048-dimensional embeddings with cosine similarity ≥ 0.999999 compared with default inference.

VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py \
  -k test_voyage_native_embedding_dimensions -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py \
  -k 'not test_embedding_gemma2 or test_embeddinggemma2_embedding_size_matches_native_dim' \
  -q

All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

## Details

Voyage's embedding head maps 1024-dimensional hidden states to 2048-dimensional embeddings. Its model adapter sets hf_config.embedding_size from num_labels, but dimension validation ignored that field and fell back to the hidden size.

The fix honors the configured embedding size and adds a regression test through LLM.embed using official model weights. The existing Extended Pooling CI task covers the test. Documentation now distinguishes output embedding size from hidden size.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Register the aten::mm out_dtype overloads for batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and an fp32 lm_head (`--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'`, which
`ModelConfig` documents as "required for RL training-inference consistency"), the head runs
`torch.mm(x, w, out_dtype=torch.float32)`. That call dispatches to `aten::mm.dtype`, a separate overload
from `aten::mm`, so on CUDA SM8x, where batch-invariant mode installs the Triton matmul overrides, it
stays on cuBLAS. Whether the result then depends on the batch size depends on the shape: on an A40,
Mistral-7B-v0.1 (vocab 32000) shows it and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (vocab 151936) do not. This PR registers
`aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` next to `aten::mm`.

## Claims

- **Bug:** on `main`, Mistral-7B-v0.1 with an fp32 head gives different logprobs at batch size 1 and 32
  for 32 of 32 prompts on an A40. In an earlier run on an A40 (`main` 34051ad714, driver 595.91.07,
  2026-10-05), Qwen3-0.6B (bs 32) and Qwen3-1.7B (bs 64) with an fp32 head showed no difference; there,
  `torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` gave the same row 0 for every M tested at N = 151936, but not at N = 4096,
  8192 or 32000.
- **Root cause:** `aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` are separate overloads of `aten::mm`, and
  `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` does not register them.
- **Fix:** one function, `mm_dtype_batch_invariant`, is registered for both overloads.
  `matmul_persistent()` takes an `out_dtype` and allocates its output in that type; the kernel already
  accumulates in fp32 and casts on store. The function keeps ATen's dtype checks for these overloads
  (for each case the same `RuntimeError` and message as `_mm_dtype_out_cuda`); shape errors still come
  from `matmul_persistent`, as with the existing `aten::mm` override.
- **Scope:** only the CUDA SM8x branch, and every `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=)` there, not just the
  lm_head. In-tree, that is also `GateLinear` tier 5 (the cuBLAS bf16→fp32 router GEMM), the non-SM90
  branch of the Inkling MoE router and the DeepSeek-V4 compressor/indexer scores. On the A40, `GateLinear`
  tier 5 was batch dependent on `main` at all four router shapes tested and is invariant with this PR.
  The lm_head runs eagerly (`compute_logits` is outside the compiled graph) and reaches `aten::mm.dtype`;
  `aten::mm.dtype_out` is what Inductor emits for the compiled callers. Hopper and Blackwell do not install
  the Triton overrides. XPU is unchanged: the fp32-head path is CUDA/ROCm only, and XPU's `aten::mm`
  override uses `matmul_descriptor_persistent`, which this PR does not touch. ROCm has no Triton matmul
  overrides on `main`; #52231 adds them and registers `aten::mm.out`, not `aten::mm.dtype`, so the same
  gap would reach ROCm when it lands.
- **Cost:** with the flag on, the fp32 head GEMM runs on the Triton persistent matmul instead of
  cuBLASLt. On the A40 that is 0.2–0.3 ms slower per call up to M=32 (Mistral-7B head shape), about the
  same at M=128 and 9% slower at M=512. It did not show in `vllm bench serve`.

## Validation

Commands, output excerpts and the full logs: [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6012055668) and
[the dtype-check follow-up](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6044314681). NVIDIA A40 (SM86), vLLM nightly wheel for
`main` `30ab428235` (`0.30.1rc1.dev708+g30ab42823`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py::test_mm_out_dtype_batch_invariance`
  fails on `main` (8166 of 8192 values of row 0 differ between M=1 and M=32) and passes with this PR.
- `test_mm_out_dtype_keeps_aten_dtype_checks`: with the flag on, invalid `out_dtype` / `out` dtypes raise
  the same errors as ATen (passes on `main` and with this PR; failed on the PR's earlier head).
- End to end, `repro_60047.py`: 32 of 32 prompts differ between batch size 1 and 32 on `main`
  (max |Δ logprob| 5.531e-05), 0 of 32 with this PR. Greedy tokens did not change in either run.
- `vllm bench serve` with the fp32 head, two runs per side (main, this PR, this PR, main): 3.87 and
  3.86 req/s on `main`, 3.86 and 3.88 req/s with this PR.

The new tests run in CI's A100 Batch Invariance job (`-k mm_out_dtype`, one line added here); the B200
job, which runs the whole file, skips them because Blackwell installs no Triton overrides.

## Details

- **Related:** #52231 (open) adds batch invariance on ROCm, including the `.out` overloads of
  mm/addmm/bmm. #59985 (open) turns `GateLinear` tier 5 off under the flag; on SM8x it overlaps with this
  PR there, without conflicting. #59952 (draft) rewrites `matmul_persistent`, and #55249, #54503, #55466
  and #60034 also edit these files, so one of them will need a small rebase.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-06 I searched all vLLM PRs for `"mm.dtype"`, `"mm.dtype_out"`,
  `out_dtype batch invariant`, `head_dtype batch invariant`, `fp32 lm_head batch invariant` and
  `logits fp32 batch invariance`; the only match is this PR.
- **Not changed:** `aten::bmm.dtype` and `aten::bmm.dtype_out` have the same gap, but no in-tree caller
  uses them.
- **Limitations:** the fix was verified end to end on one model (Mistral-7B-v0.1) on one GPU (A40). It
  was not run on A100 or XPU.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements. I reviewed every changed line and the logs.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Reuse the HF reference across use_prompt_embeds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py::test_models` builds its HuggingFace reference inside the test, and is parametrized over `use_prompt_embeds`. The reference does not depend on that parameter, so every model loads the checkpoint and decodes it once per value. This drops that repeated work from the Language Models steps.

## Change

A module-scoped fixture holds the greedy HF logprobs, keyed by every parametrized value except `use_prompt_embeds`. The key is read off `callspec.params` rather than listed by hand, so a parameter added later joins it on its own. An arm that needs only the logprobs reuses them. The `use_prompt_embeds=True` arms still load the checkpoint, since the embeddings have to come off a live reference model.

Prompt-embedding extraction moves into a helper, computing exactly what it did before. No parametrization, marker or node id changes, so every step selects the same cases as it did before, and `test_common.py` reports identical outcomes in both builds below.

Affects `Language Models (Standard)`, `(Extra Standard)` and `(Extended Generation)` on AMD and NVIDIA, and `CPU-Language Generation and Pooling Model Tests`. The three explicit node ids in `run-cpu-test-ppc64le.sh` each run in their own process, so they always miss the cache and are unchanged.

## Result

Measured against nightly build 100488 on the same commit base. The mechanism is visible as the number of completed HuggingFace checkpoint reads, which is exactly halved on AMD, the maximum available, since the `use_prompt_embeds=True` arms must still load:

| Step | HF loads, AMD | HF loads, NVIDIA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language Models (Standard) | 12 → 6 | 15 → 11 |
| Language Models (Extra Standard) | 13 → 8 | 11 → 7 |
| Language Models (Extended Generation) | 29 → 17 | 27 → 16 |

The vLLM-side load count is unchanged throughout, as expected.

For the saving, the honest figure comes from comparing only the cases where the cache actually fired (23 of them on AMD), each against its own `use_prompt_embeds=True` arm as a control for run-to-run variance. That comes to roughly 120s in Standard, 150s in Extra Standard and 480s in Extended Generation. Extended Generation carries most of it because the cache fires for all twelve of its models, the largest in the suite, with `HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B` alone worth about 170s.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fall back from DeepGEMM when nvcc is older than 12.9
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepGEMM compiles its kernels at runtime and aborts the engine when nvcc is missing or older than 12.9. vLLM only checks the GPU architecture and that DeepGEMM is installed, so on Hopper with an older toolkit, block-FP8 models crash on load. This PR adds the nvcc check, so vLLM warns and falls back to its other FP8 kernels. To find nvcc, it reuses FlashInfer's existing lookup, moved unchanged to `find_nvcc()` in `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py`.

## Claims

- Block-FP8 models load on Hopper with nvcc 12.8 or no nvcc, instead of aborting with `NVCC version must be at least 12.9`.
- The fallback logs one warning naming the nvcc version it found and where it looked.
- No change when nvcc is 12.9 or newer, or with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`.
- No change to FlashInfer: `has_flashinfer` finds the same nvcc as before, and its existing tests pass unchanged apart from the patched module.

## Validation

H100 NVL, CUDA 12.8.1 toolkit (`nvcc` 12.8), driver for CUDA 13, vLLM `528772a4b` (precompiled; `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` is identical on current main), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8`, offline `LLM.generate` with two prompts:

| | kernel selected | result |
|---|---|---|
| main | `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel` | `RuntimeError: ... NVCC version must be at least 12.9`, then `Engine core initialization failed` |
| this PR | `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | warning below, then `'The capital of France is' -> ' Paris. ...'` |

```
WARNING DeepGEMM kernels are disabled: its JIT needs nvcc 12.9 or newer (DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER, CUDA_HOME,
CUDA_PATH, PATH or /usr/local/cuda), found 12.8. Set CUDA_HOME to a newer CUDA toolkit.
```

`pytest tests/utils_/test_deep_gemm_utils.py tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py`: 7/7 (nvcc 12.8, 12.9 and 13.0; missing nvcc; the `DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER` override; FlashInfer's existing lookup tests against the shared helper).

## Details

The check finds nvcc the way DeepGEMM's JIT does (`DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER` or `DJ_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER`, then `CUDA_HOME`, `CUDA_PATH`, `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`). After the override, that is the lookup FlashInfer already had, which is why the two now share `find_nvcc()`. The check runs once, since `is_deep_gemm_supported` is cached. A fallback instead of an error matches how vLLM already handles an unsupported GPU or a missing DeepGEMM package. The cost is speed, which the warning states. On Hopper the fallback is the CUTLASS block-FP8 path.

#49051 proposed a similar check and was closed in favor of the JIT warmup RFC #47456, which does not cover the toolchain. Unlike #49051, a missing nvcc also disables DeepGEMM here, because DeepJIT has no NVRTC path: it asserts that nvcc is executable and at least 12.9 (`include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/backend.hpp` at the pinned DeepGEMM).

---

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Remove dead helpers and sync type annotations in entrypoints and config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove unreferenced dead helpers, type aliases, and unreachable branches across `vllm/entrypoints/`, correct stale docstrings and comments, and synchronize the `environment_variables` `TYPE_CHECKING` annotations with runtime defaults in `vllm/envs.py`.

Per review feedback, the deprecation helpers in `vllm/config/utils.py` are **kept**: this PR no longer touches that file (restored in faacbe2fd6). The original `SpeculativeConfig` assert simplification was superseded by #63205, which moved that logic into `NgramSpeculatorConfig.configure()`; only the docstring corrections remain for that file.

## Claims

- Removes the unused `ServeContext` dataclass and the vestigial `GenerateBaseServing.request_id_prefix` `ClassVar` in `vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py` (plus now-unused imports), and the unused `RendererRequest`/`RendererChatRequest` protocols in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/engine/typing.py` — zero remaining references (grep + mypy).
- Removes the unreachable fallback in `_parse_score_content` (`vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py`): with `wrap_dicts=False`, `parse_chat_message_content_parts` always returns `[ConversationMessage(...)]`, so the `if parse_res:` guard, the extra `create_parser()`, and the `"Only one multi-modal item is supported"` branch are dead. Behavior-preserving — the returned value is the same early-return path.
- Fixes the deprecation messages in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py` (missing space, `vllm server` -> `vllm serve`).
- Corrects stale docstrings: `prompt_lookup_min`/`prompt_lookup_max` in `vllm/config/speculative.py` (actual defaults are 5, not 1; neither is required — each defaults to the other when only one is set, per `NgramSpeculatorConfig.configure()`), `MetricSnapshot` -> `list[Metric]` in `vllm/entrypoints/llm.py`, and the `--api-key` authenticated path-prefix list in `vllm/entrypoints/common/cli_args.py` and `docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md` (`/cohere` is also authenticated).
- Synchronizes `TYPE_CHECKING` env annotations in `vllm/envs.py` with their runtime defaults (`VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`, `VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK`, `VLLM_DP_MASTER_IP`, `VLLM_XGRAMMAR_CACHE_MB`), and adds 6 missing entries.
- Updates `ignored_factors` in `compile_factors()`: adds `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB`, a frontend-only limit like the already ignored `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB`, and removes `VLLM_CPU_MOE_PREPACK`, which is not in `environment_variables` so this is a no-op. The `torch.compile` cache key changes once on upgrade.

## Validation

- **Test commands run:**
  ```bash
  pre-commit run --files \
    vllm/config/speculative.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/serve/engine/typing.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/common/cli_args.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/llm.py \
    vllm/envs.py \
    docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md
  ```
- **Results:** All hooks (`ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `mypy` on the oldest supported Python, `validate-config`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-root-lazy-imports`, `check-forbidden-imports`) passed.
- **Behavior:** No request-handling behavior change — removals are unreferenced symbols or provably unreachable branches (see Claims); the `envs.py` changes are `TYPE_CHECKING`-only, except the one-time `compile_factors()` cache key change above.
- **Model evaluation:** N/A (dead-code removal and comment/annotation sync).

## Details

- **Motivation:** A repository sweep of `vllm/entrypoints/` and `vllm/config/` found helpers left behind after earlier refactors with zero remaining references.
- **Review response:** The concern about deleting the `vllm/config/utils.py` deprecation helpers was addressed by restoring them unchanged (commit faacbe2fd6) — they are the standard machinery for future config/env deprecation windows.
- **Duplicate-PR check:** Searched open PRs for these symbols and areas; no overlapping open PR.
- **AI assistance:** AI assistance was used to audit unreferenced symbols and prepare this PR; all changes were reviewed and verified locally.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Do not retry safetensors metadata lookup in offline mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Fixes #66006.

When `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, calling `hf_api().get_safetensors_metadata(...)` raises `huggingface_hub.errors.OfflineModeIsEnabled`. In `try_get_safetensors_metadata`, `with_retry` was not including `OfflineModeIsEnabled` in `fatal_errors`, treating it as a transient failure and attempting retries with a 2-second sleep delay and logging two spurious `ERROR` messages before falling back to reading the cached snapshot headers.

This PR adds `OfflineModeIsEnabled` to `fatal_errors`, allowing offline mode to raise immediately and proceed straight to the local cache fallback without retry delays or error logs.

## Claims
- Eliminates spurious `ERROR ... offline mode is enabled` logs during offline speculative draft model initialization.
- Eliminates the 2-second retry sleep during startup in offline mode.
- Immediately proceeds to reading metadata from the pre-populated local cache snapshot.

## Validation
- Added `test_safetensors_metadata_offline_mode_does_not_retry` to `tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py` asserting that `get_safetensors_metadata` is called exactly once when `OfflineModeIsEnabled` is raised.
- Ran tests in `tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py`.
- Formatted and linted with `ruff check` and `ruff format`.

## Details
In `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`, `try_get_safetensors_metadata` wraps the Hub metadata call with `with_retry(..., fatal_errors=(huggingface_hub.errors.NotASafetensorsRepoError,))`. In offline mode, the error is definitive rather than transient. Adding `huggingface_hub.errors.OfflineModeIsEnabled` to `fatal_errors` ensures immediate failure without logging or delay, which is then cleanly handled by `except Exception: return None` so `get_safetensors_params_metadata` proceeds directly to `snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`.

---

commits.pr_title: [Model] Use the upstream config for Qwen3-ASR
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Deletes the vendored `Qwen3ASRConfig` and loads Qwen3-ASR through the upstream class, flattening `thinker_config` for original checkpoints. Prerequisite for #65735, which replaces #62398.

## Claims

- Original and Transformers-format checkpoints now resolve to one config class, so a native load no longer registers a class that hijacks `-hf` checkpoints in the same process.
- `classify_num` becomes the upstream `num_labels`, and the forced aligner architecture is set while flattening, so `Qwen3ASRModelArchConfigConvertor` is gone.
- No change in what vLLM builds or outputs for the five checkpoints below.

## Validation

| Checkpoint | Model dump diffs | Output, before vs after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` | 0 | Identical |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B` | 0 | Identical |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B` | 0 | Identical |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-hf` | 0 | Identical |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf` | 0 | Not run |

Outputs are greedy token IDs on two audio assets (time bins for the aligner), on Transformers 5.23.0.dev0 and one B200 GPU. The GPU runs used an older base commit (9b34fec) because of the precompiled extensions there. Config loading was also checked on the 5.16.1 floor.

```bash
S=.agents/skills/transformers-upgrade/scripts
for dump in dump_configs dump_model; do
    PYTHONPATH=<base> python $S/$dump.py before.jsonl <repos>
    PYTHONPATH=$PWD python $S/$dump.py after.jsonl <repos>
    python $S/diff_dumps.py before.jsonl after.jsonl
done
pytest tests/transformers_utils tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_asr.py \
    tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_asr_mrope.py
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k Qwen3ASR
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Qwen3ASR
```

All pass, except `test_dspark_draft_loads_weights`, which also fails on `main`.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Document multimodal requirements for the Transformers modeling …
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Documents what a custom model needs to run multimodal input through the Transformers modeling backend, as suggested by @hmellor in #36864. I hit most of these while running OmniASR (`ziywang50/omniASR-LLM-300M-hf`, remote code) through the backend.

## Claims

- "Custom models": `auto_map.AutoModel` must point to the base model.
- "Writing custom models": a new step 4, "If your model is multimodal", covering the nested text config, `get_<modality>_features`, and the processor's placeholder token.
- Docs only, no code changes. Updated with @hmellor's review suggestions.

## Validation

vLLM paths are under `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/` at `0b5a44fe08` unless noted. Transformers references are by function name, since line numbers vary between versions.

**`auto_map.AutoModel` must point to the base model**

- The backend creates the wrapped model with `AutoModel.from_config(...)` and stores it as `self.model` (`base.py` L180, L231-233).
- For remote code, `AutoModel.from_config` instantiates the class named in `config.auto_map["AutoModel"]` (Transformers `_BaseAutoModelClass.from_config`).
- The backend then adds its own `lm_head` (`causal.py` L48).
- The weight name mapping is built from the direct children of `self.model` (`base.py` L315-356), so it also assumes `self.model` is the base model.

So if `AutoModel` points to the model with the head, the backend wraps a model that already has an `lm_head`, and the checkpoint names no longer line up with the module names. OmniASR needed this change to run with the backend (ziywang50/omniasr-hf@fefab6b).

**1. The config must nest the text config**

- Suggested by @hmellor in review: `_get_transformers_backend_cls` only adds `MultiModal` to the class name when `hf_config is not hf_text_config` (`vllm/config/model.py` L1147-1148), so a flat config silently gets the text-only class.

**2. `get_<modality>_features` on the base model, with `return_dict=True` and `pooler_output`**

- Audio: `self.model.get_audio_features(input_features, return_dict=True, ...)`, then `.pooler_output` (`multimodal.py` L1070-1073, and L1079-1087 for un-padded audio). The output is split per item by the placeholder counts (`_split_embeddings`, L1005; counts from L835).
- Vision inputs (`pixel_values`): `_get_features` looks the method up by name, `getattr(self.model, f"get_{modality}_features")`, calls it with `return_dict=True` and returns `.pooler_output` (L1167-1181).
- Images and videos: `_process_vision_input` passes `"image"` or `"video"` to `_get_features` (L1103, L1115), which looks the method up with `getattr(self.model, f"get_{modality}_features")` (no default), calls it with `return_dict=True` and returns `.pooler_output` (L1167-1181).

**3. The processor must define `<modality>_token` and reach `get_text_with_replacements`**

- As @hmellor pointed out in review, `_get_prompt_updates` reads `<modality>_token` with no default (`getattr(hf_processor, f"{modality}_token")`, L697).
- In Transformers, `ProcessorMixin.__call__` returns the offsets computed by `get_text_with_replacements`. `_process_audio` builds one replacement per item by calling `replace_audio_token`, and only does so when `audio_token` is set; the default `replace_<modality>_token` raises `NotImplementedError`.
- The backend asks the processor for `return_text_replacement_offsets` (L774) and raises when a request with multi-modal data gets none back (L798-810), so a processor without `<modality>_token` fails here too.
- vLLM also reads `processor.audio_token` to build the dummy text (`get_dummy_text`, L321-323).

## Details

For built-in models, `AutoModel` comes from Transformers' own mapping (e.g. `glmasr` → `GlmAsrModel`), so they are not affected. Remote-code repos sometimes map it to the full model instead (e.g. `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`): that works in Transformers, but not with the backend, and nothing warns about it. OmniASR's first version did the same.

Dropped per review: the audio length item, since a missing field already raises a `ValueError` naming the config class and all three attributes (`get_max_audio_tokens`, L191-202).

Not included: when the number of embeddings doesn't match the placeholders, `_split_embeddings` only logs a warning and pads or truncates (`multimodal.py` L1022-1035, with a TODO to make it an error). I didn't hit this, so I left it out, but I'm happy to add a line if you think it belongs here.

I used Claude to help read the code and draft the wording, and checked every reference above against the code myself.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Keep Ray metrics usable without Ray Serve
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Import optional Ray Serve separately from Ray metrics.
- Keep `RayPrometheusStatLogger` usable when Ray is installed without the Serve extra.
- Fall back to an empty `ReplicaId` when no Serve replica context is available.

## Context

`RayPrometheusStatLogger` only uses Ray Serve to retrieve a replica ID. If `ray.serve` fails to import because `ray[serve]` dependencies are absent, the shared `try` block also discards the successful `ray.util.metrics` import. Metric construction then raises the misleading error that Ray is not installed.

This is the vLLM-side counterpart to ray-project/ray#67444. That change fixes one Serve-extra import failure in Ray. vLLM should still keep its Ray metrics independent from optional Serve dependencies.

## Duplicate check

I searched open vLLM PRs and issues for `ray_wrappers`, the `RayPrometheusMetric requires Ray to be installed` error, and Ray Serve extras. I found no existing change that separates these imports.

## Tests

- `/home/ubuntu/work/vllm-main/.venv/bin/python` smoke check with `ray.serve` unavailable and `ray.util.metrics` available: passed. Constructed a `RayCounterWrapper` and verified its tags were `{"ReplicaId": ""}`.
- `/home/ubuntu/work/vllm-main/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py`: passed, including ruff, mypy, and repository checks.

## AI assistance

I used OpenAI Codex to help implement and test this change. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Use embedding_dim for pooling output size
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60977.

`ModelConfig.embedding_size` can report the transformer hidden size instead of the final embedding width for pooling models with an output projection.

For `google/embeddinggemma-2`, this results in a reported size of 512 instead of 768, causing `PoolingParams(dimensions=768)` to fail validation.

## Claims

This change uses `embedding_dim` as a fallback for pooling models before falling back to `hidden_size`.

The existing precedence for explicit `embedding_size` values and Sentence-Transformers Dense modules is preserved. Generation runners are unaffected.

## Validation

**Tests**

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_pooling_params.py
# 14 passed
```

Added network-free tests:

- `test_pooling_embedding_dim_preferred_over_hidden_size_without_network`
- `test_matryoshka_accepts_native_embedding_width_without_network`

These cover the `embedding_dim` fallback, override/Dense/generate precedence, and Matryoshka dims 128/256/512/768 (with 0/769 rejected).

**GPU reproduction (RTX A5000)**

| Dimensions | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default | 768 | 768 |
| 128 | Pass | Pass |
| 256 | Pass | Pass |
| 512 | Pass | Pass |
| 768 | Validation error | Pass |
| 769 | Rejected | Rejected |

The resulting embeddings were also compared against Hugging Face, with cosine similarity ≥ 0.99997 in the tested cases.

Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

## Details

The current fallback in `ModelConfig.embedding_size` uses `get_hidden_size()` when neither an explicit override nor a Sentence-Transformers Dense module is available.

That assumption doesn't hold for models such as EmbeddingGemma 2, where a final projection changes the embedding width.

The patch checks `hf_text_config.embedding_dim` (or top-level `embedding_dim`) for pooling runners before using the hidden size.

Other pooling models exposing this configuration field may also be affected; EmbeddingGemma 2 is the reproduced case.

The unrelated Triton shared-memory issue #60847 is outside the scope of this PR.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and testing.

commits.pr_title: [torch.compile] Replace config `compute_hash` with `compile_factors`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replaces every config's `compute_hash() -> str` with `compile_factors() -> dict`, covering the remaining TODOs in #39479.

Closes #39479 It revives #40246, which was approved but closed when its branch was deleted, rebased onto current main.

## Claims

- Configs return their compile factors; `normalize_value` uses a nested config's `compile_factors()`, so `CompilationConfig` and `KernelConfig` no longer special-case `pass_config`, `dynamic_shapes_config` or `ir_op_priority`.
- `hash_config()` / `hash_config_cached()` replace `compute_hash()` / `compute_hash_cached()` for callers that need a string (EPLB, DP validation, serve fingerprint, startup plan, FlashInfer autotune cache).
- `cache_key_factors.json` now records the full env, config, code and compiler factors, not just env factors and hashes.
- JIT (`VllmBackend`) and AOT (`aot_compile_hash_factors`) share one env/config hash helper, and the JIT cache key and AOT source check share one code hashing helper. `CompilationConfig.traced_files` is now `set[Path]`.
- Every config that affects the graph is now opt-out: it hashes all fields except an explicit `ignored_factors` set, so new fields are hashed by default. Configs that don't affect the graph return `{}` and say how to switch if that changes.
- `get_compile_factors` raises on unknown `ignored_factors`, so a typo can't silently leave a field hashed.
- The set of hashed fields is unchanged, but hash values change, so existing compile caches miss once.
- **Breaking for out-of-tree code:** `additional_config` objects and `CompilerInterface` subclasses must implement `compile_factors()` instead of `compute_hash()`. A `CompilerInterface` subclass still defining `compute_hash` raises `TypeError`, since it would otherwise silently drop out of the cache key (for example `AscendCompiler` in vllm-ascend).
- The worker sentinel now uses `hash_config_cached`, like every other EPLB `model_states` lookup, avoiding a `KeyError` after `max_model_len` auto-fit.
- Supersedes #62458, #61885 and #62628.

## Validation

B200, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` loaded twice with an empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`:

| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| Warm start loads compiled artifacts | yes | yes |
| Greedy output | `' Paris. The capital of France is also…'` | identical |
| `cache_key_factors.json` keys | `env` + 3 hashes | `env`, `config` (per sub-config), `code`, `compiler` + 3 hashes |
| Compile and config tests (989) | 21 fail | the same 21 fail |

The 21 failures are all in `tests/compile/test_config.py` and also fail on main on this host: cudagraph capture-size defaults for B200, plus a forked `test_VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE[1]` subprocess exiting with status 3.

```bash
python cache_run.py Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B $VLLM_CACHE_ROOT  # LLM(...).generate twice, then read cache_key_factors.json
pytest tests/compile/test_config.py tests/compile/fullgraph/test_toy_llama.py tests/compile/fullgraph/test_simple.py \
  tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multiple_graphs.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py tests/compile/test_decorator.py tests/config tests/test_config.py
```

```bash
pytest tests/config tests/test_config.py tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_fingerprint.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/compile/test_config.py
```

Tests: main and branch give identical results on these suites on macOS (1105 passed; the same 63 fail on both for environment reasons). New tests in `tests/config/test_config_utils.py` cover nested-config hashing and unknown `ignored_factors`.

commits.pr_title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by subclassing mocked torch classes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The strict docs build on main has failed since #65235 with `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand` and `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'PydanticMagicMock'` ([main build at #65235](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35689810/)). Every main build since then fails the same way. PRs that change docs fail too, while PRs without docs changes skip the build.

## Claims

- Fixes the strict docs build. The argparse docs generator imports every CLI subcommand again, including `vllm preload`.
- Generated CLI and engine-args pages are unchanged.

## Validation

`mkdocs build --strict` in a docs-only environment, as on Read the Docs (`requirements/docs.txt`, Python 3.12, no torch):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .docs-venv
uv pip install --python .docs-venv/bin/python -r requirements/docs.txt
.docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --strict --config-file mkdocs.yaml --site-dir /tmp/site
```

| `generate_argparse.py` | Result |
|---|---|
| main | exit 1, `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand`, same `TypeError` as the Read the Docs log |
| this PR | exit 0, all CLI pages built, including `cli/preload` |

## Details

- Root cause: `TraceTensor` subclasses `torch.Tensor`, which is mocked in the docs build. Subclassing a mock produced a mock instance rather than a class, and `@dataclass` then failed on the `Copy.src: TraceTensor` annotation in `reload/bake.py`.
- Fix: `PydanticMagicMock.__mro_entries__` gives any class inheriting from a mock a real `MockBase` base, so it is a real type. `MockBase` supports pydantic schemas and subscripting (for `cachetools.LRUCache[_K, _V]`). `torch.nn` now uses `PydanticMagicMock`, so `nn.*` subclasses are covered too.
- Validated with `mkdocs build --strict` on current main without torch: exit 0, no warnings. Compared with the previous fix, the page set is identical. `cli/bench/serve` differs only in its random `--result-filename` default and the order of a `set` of choices.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `generate_argparse.py` or this failure. #66044 fixed unrelated cross-reference warnings.

commits.pr_title: [MOE oracle][Refactor][1/N] Deduplicate the MoE oracle selection and backend code
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

**Refactor only: line changes in production (non-test) code +449/-756 (net -307 vs origin/main 3fe0d44219); the only behavioural differences are the oracle log and `ValueError` text, the per-candidate DEBUG rejection logging, and the new activation-format check, listed in `## Claims`.**

## Overview

This PR removes code duplicate in MOE oracles as per https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37753. This PR continues #43461 work on `MoEKernelOracle` to share more oracle logic.

Previously, every oracle module carried its own copy of the same two things, and the copies had drifted (`is_monolithic` computed two ways, `use_monolithic` missing from the W4A8 tail, the monolithic-only guard only in W4A8 INT8).

This PR abstracts:

- `_make_log_backend` / `_make_log_unsupported` (7 copies) → the `MoEKernelOracle` methods `make_log_backend()` / `make_log_unsupported()`
- `_return_or_raise` (7 copies) → the `MoEKernelOracle` methods `return_or_raise()` / `try_backend()` (the probe itself, which logs every rejected candidate as the pre-refactor loops did)
- prepare/finalize → experts → `FusedMoEKernel` assembly (8 copies under `oracle/`, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py#L855-L903) → `make_moe_kernel()`
- mxfp8's own `Using '…' MxFp8 MoE backend` lines and rejection message → the same helpers

Per-oracle differences become arguments (`input_dtype`, `per_token_activation`, `b_strides1/2` + `group_size`, the WNA16 `allowed_experts` assert, the W4A8 INT8 guard). Each oracle class declares `name` and forwards `backend_to_kernel_cls` to its module's function at call time, and one instance carries the deployment inputs of a selection (`moe_config`, `weight_key`, `activation_key`), with the prepare/finalize layout read from `FusedMoEConfig.activation_format`. That is what collapses the call sites to one or two lines and gives the auto-selection loops one probe; `w4a8` keeps its own loop, as it has no oracle class here.

## Claims

- No public function is renamed or re-signatured; selection outcomes and the kwargs handed to prepare/finalize and to the experts constructors are identical. One exception: Standard-only experts (W4A8, W4A8 INT8) behind a `BatchedExperts` prepare/finalize now raise `ValueError` in `make_moe_kernel` instead of `TypeError`; that pairing already failed in `FusedMoEKernel._post_init_setup`, so no working configuration changes.
- `use_monolithic` is `experts_cls.is_monolithic()` everywhere (W4A8 previously relied on the implicit `False`), equivalent to the previous mix with `issubclass(..., FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic)` for every in-tree experts class.
- `try_backend()` logs one DEBUG line per rejected candidate class, as the pre-refactor per-oracle loops did, so a multi-candidate backend (the Monolithic/Modular pairs, Humming's three) keeps the reason each class lost rather than only the last one. The explicit `--moe-backend` path now emits those lines too before `return_or_raise()` raises; it logged nothing there before, and this is DEBUG-only. It also returns the full `(kernel_cls, reason)` rejection list, so the MXFP4 "no backend supports this configuration" `NotImplementedError` still reports one reason per candidate rather than one per backend.
- `backend_to_kernel_cls` is a plain instance method on each oracle class (same shape as `MoEKernelOracle` and the unquantized oracle) forwarding to the module-level function at call time, rather than a `= staticmethod(<module fn>)` import-time snapshot. The module-level function therefore stays the single source of truth: patching it still changes selection, which is the upstream idiom the quantization backends and the tests use, and it is why `test_cutlass_moe.py`, `test_ocp_mx_moe.py` and `test_gfx950_moe.py` keep their original module-level `monkeypatch.setattr` and are not part of this diff. `_requested_kernel_cls` calls the module-level function directly, as before the refactor.
- `activation_format` is not state on the oracle: it is read from the `FusedMoEConfig.activation_format` property where the probe needs it, so the duplicated per-module derivations collapse onto that one definition.
- `make_moe_kernel` pairs the experts class with the prepare/finalize on `experts_cls.activation_format().is_superset(prepare_finalize.activation_format)` rather than equality, matching `FusedMoEExperts.is_supported_config`, so a `PaddedStandard` (DeepEP v2) experts class can be paired with a `Standard` prepare/finalize.
- New coverage: the helpers' message text, first-supported probing and the returned rejection list, each oracle class resolving its own backend→kernel-class list, the prepare/finalize + experts kwargs for 6 of the 8 oracles, the format-mismatch rejection with the `is_superset` direction in both directions, and the `FusedMoEConfig.activation_format` prediction including `batched_triton` (64 cases).
- `MoEKernelOracle`'s six not-yet-migrated methods raise `NotImplementedError` and are no longer `@abstractmethod`, so the per-oracle classes are instantiable; restoring the contract is #37753. Activation keys stay typed via the `cast(QuantKey | None, object())` sentinel, and no oracle is mutated after construction.

Left to other PRs, preferably standalone:
- [ ] Humming `make_humming_moe_kernel` https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/humming/moe.py#L224-L300 is not updated, being done in #57538.
- [ ] Sharing the per-oracle priority/env policy that still precedes the shared `try_backend` probe in each `select_*_moe_backend`.
- [ ] Re-introducing the `(key, was_set)` MoE activation override lookup where it belongs, with a real `QuantSpec.fields_set` (#59438 / #51808): that distinction requires changing the `weight`/`activation` defaults to a sentinel and updating every reader of those fields, so it stays out of this refactor and mxfp4 keeps its local `_user_moe_activation_override() -> QuantKey | None`. **=> #51808 was merged so this should be done as a next step**
- [ ] Decide on `@abstractmethod` usage as per #37753 in a future PR - out of scope for now.
- [ ] Migrate `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/w4a8.py`
- [ ] Extending the per-oracle `MoEKernelOracle` classes with the rest of the oracle logic and restoring `@abstractmethod`, as the follow-up to #37753:
    - [ ] `select_*_moe_backend`
    - [ ] `convert_to_*_moe_kernel_format` (still near-1k-line `if/else` bodies)
    - [ ] turning each module's 10-way `backend_to_kernel_cls` `if/else` into a table (it is forwarded from the class now, but still written per module)
- [ ] `int_wna16` and `w4a8_int8` are not rows of the parametrized assembly test because their entry points assert concrete experts classes. The W4A8 INT8 assembly kwargs are therefore covered only by inspection here: `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_int4_moe.py` is gated to Arm CPU builds (`current_platform.is_cpu() and get_cpu_architecture() == CpuArchEnum.ARM`) and this node is an x86 host running a ROCm torch build, so the file skips by design rather than for lack of CPU access.

## Validation

Tests ran on commit 2101a916d9 in this PR's container: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0.0 (`/opt/rocm/.info/version` = `7.15.26333-0000000`), clang 23.0.0git.

### New tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py -q
```
```
64 passed, 14 warnings in 0.58s
```

### Impacted tests

Every test file that reaches the changed code, minus the model-download case:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py \
  --deselect tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_mxfp4_loading_and_execution_moe \
  -q
```
=> `142 passed, 515 skipped, 5 deselected, 14 warnings in 32.33s.`

With the new test file in the same selection: `206 passed, 515 skipped, 5 deselected, 14 warnings in 33.43s.`

The oracle-adjacent selection suites that reach the same helpers (`tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`, including its LoRA cases) also pass: `47 passed, 3 skipped`.

No model evaluation was run: the change re-routes the same arguments and does not touch backend selection, kernel construction or numerics.

## Details

- Reviewers should focus on `MoEKernelOracle.return_or_raise`: it is now the single place deciding whether an explicitly requested `--moe-backend` is accepted, and it forwards `(backend, kernel class, weight_key, activation_key, activation_format)` to `is_supported_config`. A mistake there silently changes which kernel runs instead of failing a test.
- The explicit-backend test tolerates two outcomes on purpose: either the mapped backend is returned, or the rejection message must name the mapped backend. That keeps it platform-agnostic while still catching a dropped or remapped override.
- No documentation change: nothing under `docs/` references these helpers or the log strings.
- `tests/quantization/test_online.py` now patches `maybe_make_prepare_finalize` where it is actually called (`oracle.base`), since the prepare/finalize is built by the shared `make_moe_kernel` rather than per oracle. The test is gated on the FlashInfer dispatch-format API, so it skips on this node.
- The five log / `ValueError` text changes, all in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/`: `Using 'X' …` becomes `Using X …` for WNA16/mxfp4/nvfp4/mxfp8 and rejections carrying a reason quote the backend value (fp8/int8/unquantized/W4A8 INT8/mxfp8); `FP8 MoE backend …` becomes `Fp8 MoE backend '…'`; mxfp8's `No supported MXFP8 expert class for …: reason` becomes the shared rejection message and its explicit path loses the `(user-requested)` hint; the explicit `scope="local"` arguments in WNA16/mxfp4 are dropped (`"local"` is the `vllm/logger.py` default, so the dedup key is unchanged); the `out of potential backends: […]` suffix now appears on `return_or_raise` paths that previously omitted it (unquantized MOONEP, nvfp4 explicit) while WNA16/mxfp4 still omit it, so "uniform wording" holds per message, not per oracle. Because the shared helpers emit from `oracle/base.py`, rejection lines now carry the `…oracle.base` logger and a `base.py` source line, while the `Using …` lines still come from each oracle's own logger.

This is not a duplicate of the closed #44562 / #46901 / #54290 / #54294, which added per-oracle subclasses that only delegated and left the duplicated code in place; here the duplicated code is gone and the subclasses carry only `name` and `backend_to_kernel_cls`, with #37753 continuing the migration of the remaining oracle logic onto them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 vision crash with online FP8 quantization
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63732. With `--quantization fp8`, an image request to Gemma 4 returns HTTP 500 and kills the engine core. The transformers patch embedder casts the pixel values to `input_proj.weight.dtype`. Once vLLM quantizes that layer, this dtype is `float8_e4m3fn`, so the FP8 linear gets an FP8 input. This PR runs the patch embedder steps in `gemma4_mm.py` with the pixel values cast to `self.model_dtype`. It makes the same change for the pooled states before `embedding_projection` in the encoder CUDA graph path.

Compared with #63911, this fix:

- Also fixes `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model`. They borrow Gemma 4's `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` and build their own FP8-quantized tower. [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) swaps the embedder only in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.__init__`, so their image and video paths still crash with the reported error (checked with a probe that loads E4B with FP8 and builds each model's own tower, since no checkpoint of either model was at hand).
- Adds tests that fail on the old code for video and for the encoder CUDA graph path, including the `embedding_projection` cast. The compiled and encoder-graph cases in [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) pass on the old code, so they guard neither path.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image requests with online FP8 no longer crash the engine. `input_proj` stays FP8 and still uses the same FP8 kernel.
- The same fix covers video inputs. On the old code, `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` with video enabled crashed at engine start, because the encoder profile run sends dummy video through the same patch embedder.
- The same fix covers the encoder CUDA graph path (the patch embedder call and the `embedding_projection` cast).
- Online `fp8_per_block`, `fp8_per_channel` and `mxfp8` (eager, custom ops off) crashed at engine start on the old code. With this fix, all three answer `The sign in the image is a **STOP** sign.`
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model` get the same fix through the borrowed methods.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 1 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 16 GB (SM 12.0), vLLM `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`) with and without this patch, transformers 5.20.2.

Reproducer. Server:

```bash
vllm serve --port 18000 --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}'
```

Once it logs `Application startup complete`, send a 64x64 white PNG:

```bash
BODY='{"model":"google/gemma-4-E4B-it","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAAABACAIAAAAlC+aJAAAAS0lEQVR42u3PMQ0AAAwDoPo33UrYvQQckD4XAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAYHLAMpT0sIcNbcEAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"}},{"type":"text","text":"What color is this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":16}'
OUT=$(curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}' localhost:18000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY")
echo "$OUT"
echo "IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
```

Before (3 of 3 runs, each on a fresh server): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=500`. The server log shows:

```
RuntimeError: ... "dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant_kernel_scalar_type" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

After (6 of 6 runs, each on a fresh server: 3 by me and 3 in a separate re-check): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=200`, answer `"The image is **white**."`. No `not implemented`, `Traceback` or `EngineDeadError` line in any log. The server still selects `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod`. The old code gives the same answer only when `input_proj` is left out of FP8 with `--quantization-config '{"ignore":["vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj"]}'`.

New tests, on the old `gemma4_mm.py` and on this patch:

 | Test | Old code | This PR |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py -k gemma4` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k gemma4_fp8` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |

On the old code, the CUDA graph row fails earlier, in the eager video profile run. So I also checked each CUDA graph change on its own: with only the `encoder_cudagraph_forward` patch-embedder call reverted, or only the old `embedding_projection.weight.dtype` cast restored, the row fails with the same error.

Borrowing models: a script builds a vision tower with random weights from the E4B config (unquantized) and calls `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` on all three classes. Image and video outputs for all three match the old code exactly (same shapes and sums).

`pre-commit run` on the four changed files passes.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM builds the Gemma 4 vision tower with `AutoModel.from_config`. It then replaces each `nn.Linear` with a `ReplicatedLinear` that carries the tower quant config. With online FP8, `input_proj.weight` becomes `float8_e4m3fn` after loading. The transformers `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.forward` does:

```python
pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
if (target_dtype := self.input_proj.weight.dtype).is_floating_point:
    pixel_values = pixel_values.to(target_dtype)
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values)
```

This is right for a plain `nn.Linear`. For a quantized layer, though, the weight dtype is the storage dtype. FP8 is a floating type, so the guard lets the cast through. The bf16 pixel values are rounded to FP8 without a scale, and the FP8 linear's activation quant gets an FP8 input. `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` only accepts fp16, bf16 or fp32. A debug run confirmed the chain: the pixel values enter the patch embedder as bf16, and only `vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj` receives an FP8 input. `encoder_cudagraph_forward` had the same mistake in vLLM code: it cast the pooled states to `embedding_projection.weight.dtype`, which is also FP8 under the tower quant config.

The CUDA kernel runs when the `quant_fp8` custom op is on: with `--enforce-eager`, with `+quant_fp8`, and by vLLM's default for block-scaled FP8 checkpoints and ROCm AITER FP8 linear. With the op off, eager `forward_native` also fails (`"abs_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'`). Only the default compile mode passes without an error, and there the pixel values are still rounded to FP8 without a scale.

Fix: a module-level `_embed_patches(patch_embedder, pixel_values, pixel_position_ids, padding_positions, dtype)` repeats the steps of the transformers forward (`2 * (x - 0.5)`, `input_proj`, `_position_embeddings`, sum), but casts to the given dtype. The image, video and encoder CUDA graph paths call it with `self.model_dtype`. The CUDA graph path also casts the pooled states to `self.model_dtype`, as the eager paths already do before `embed_vision`. The quant config is not touched, so the layers stay FP8. For an unquantized layer nothing changes, because then the weight dtype is the model dtype. The helper is a module-level function, not a method, because the two borrowing models copy `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` without inheriting from Gemma 4. A method would be missing on those classes.

Alternatives not taken:

- Building `input_proj` without quantization: this changes which layers the user's quantization covers. It can also break loading of pre-quantized checkpoints that quantize this layer, and it leaves the `embedding_projection` cast as it is.
- Making the FP8 linear accept an FP8 input: this treats the crash site, and by then the input has already been rounded to FP8.

Tradeoffs and limitations:

- `_embed_patches` uses the private `_position_embeddings` of the transformers embedder. This file already splits `Gemma4VisionModel.forward` into its parts, so this goes one level deeper in the same style.
- With online FP8 in the default compile mode, which did not crash before, image outputs may change a little because the pixel values are no longer rounded to FP8 first. On `input_proj` against the bf16 weight, the relative error went from 4.50% to 3.68%. I did not run a vision eval.
- The tests use `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, which CI already uses. E2B has the same vision tower and would be cheaper, but I could not confirm the answer checks (`stop`, `book`) on E2B.
- CI: `gemma4_mm.py` is added to `source_file_dependencies` of `quantized-models-test` and its AMD mirror, so the eager test runs when this file changes. This adds an estimated 14% more runs of that step. The `gemma4_fp8` row (`core_model`) runs in the existing multimodal step.
- Not run on AMD.
- Out of scope: online `mxfp4` on SM 12.x fails at engine start in `input_proj` with `ValueError: SM12x cute-dsl requires NVFP4 with 128x4 scales`, the same before and after this patch, with a bf16 input.

---

commits.pr_title: [CI] Run PyTorch Compilation root tests in one pytest, with test_config.py's forked tests spawned
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Runs the PyTorch Compilation root tests (`tests/compile/test_*.py`) in one plain pytest instead of the `find | xargs` loop, and enrolls the step and its AMD mirror in `automatic_shard`. To make one process safe, `test_config.py`'s seven `@pytest.mark.forked` tests now spawn instead of fork, and the three test files that set the default device reset it when the file ends. Alternative to #65476; only one should merge.

## Claims

| Job | Before | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| `pytorch-compilation-unit-tests` | one job, one pytest per file | one job, one pytest |
| its AMD mirror | one job, one pytest per file | one job, one pytest |

- Every test runs exactly once, with the same outcome as on main.
- A new root test file runs without a YAML edit, as with today's `find` loop (`--ignore-glob='compile/*/*'` leaves subdirectories to their own steps). Collecting the directory also picks up root `*_test.py` files, pytest's other default pattern; none exist today.
- The step stays under the 20-minute target, setup included. The mirror doesn't, and neither does main's: main 100329 ran it in 20.4 min three commits before this base, this PR in 20.3 (see Validation). **This needs a timing exception for the mirror.**
- Both plan one job today and split by themselves once their tests outgrow one.

## Validation

`/ci run` build 100354 on this head (the bot merged main cb95d994f4 into it first), against main 100317 for the step and main 100329 for the mirror. Nothing under `tests/compile`, `tests/utils.py`, `vllm/compilation` or the step's YAML changed between 100317 and cb95d994f4.

| | Node IDs (passed / skipped) | Missing / added / outcome changed | Job, setup included | Machine time vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the step | 225 (223 / 2), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 18.3 min (main 21.2) | -14% |
| its AMD mirror | 225 (221 / 4), same as main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 20.3 min (main 20.4) | -1% |

- **Mirror runtime on main:** the last 19 passed main builds (100087-100282) ran it in 19.5-23.3 min, median 19.8, with two over 20 (20.6 and 23.3). Main 100329 (6128b9072d, three commits before this base) ran it in 20.4 min; this PR's run took 20.3. The planner adds main's per-test times and the job's measured setup (about 18 min in all) but not pytest's startup and collection, so it plans one job. The job runs the same tests as on main.
- **Step runtime on main:** 16.2-21.8 min in the 8 of those builds that ran it, two over 20.
- Wall time is each job's start to finish: queue excluded; checkout, image pull and setup included. No automatic retries; the whole build passed. Earlier runs gave the same 225 node IDs at 18.6 / 20.6 min (100169) and 19.1 / 20.2 min (100335, with the previous version's conftest fixture).
- The other compile steps this change triggers (the AMD Dynamic Shapes, Passes, H100 Cases, Fullgraph and Fullgraph CUDAGraph jobs) match main 100329 node for node.
- Without the test change, one pytest fails: build [99664](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99664) had 12 `test_config.py` failures with `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`, and the mirror hung in the same file.
- `split_check.py` finds no step whose jobs each run the whole suite.

## Details

- **Root cause (#28965):** pytest-forked always uses `os.fork`, so `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` didn't help. `create_new_process_for_each_test("spawn")` runs the test in a fresh interpreter (already the default on ROCm), imports the test's module there so counters like `compilation_counter` stay the real ones, and re-raises the child's failure or skip in the parent.
- **Default device:** `test_compile_ranges.py`, `test_graph_partition.py` and `test_structured_logging.py` call `torch.set_default_device` and leave it set; in one process that would move later files' tensors onto the GPU. Each of the three files gets a module-scoped autouse fixture that resets it when that file ends. Inside each file nothing changes (later tests there, such as the CUDA-only graph partition tests, still run on the device as on main), and `tests/compile/conftest.py` is untouched, so no other step's tests are affected.
- **Known limit:** other process-wide state could still leak between files; a pass shows the current order works, not every order.
- **Versus #65476:** that PR keeps one process per file and changes no test code, but a new root file then needs a YAML line or it doesn't run.
- **If the exception isn't OK:** test cases can't be split under 20 here, since no single test is long and the plan already fits one job. Moving `test_aot_compile.py` (about 10 of the mirror's 17 pytest minutes) to its own step would bring both jobs to about 12 minutes, for one more job's setup.
- **Timeouts unchanged.** `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job.

commits.pr_title: [Build][Bugfix] Never fall back from an x.yf CUDA arch to a lower minor
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the CUDA arch selection so an `x.yf` (family) source arch never falls back to a lower minor of the same major. Before this change, `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` mapped `10.7f` onto a plain `10.0` target. With CUDA >= 13.4 and an arch list without 10.7, such as the cu134 release list, this compiled the LUT-B MoE kernel from #62759 for `sm_100`, and ptxas rejected it.

The first version of this PR filtered only the LUT-B arch list. This version fixes the shared function instead and removes that filter.

## Claims

- The family fallback for `x.yf` now only takes a target with the same major and a version >= `x.y`. It tries the highest `x.y` first. `12.0f` still matches `12.1a`. `10.7f` no longer matches `10.0`, `10.0a` or `10.0f`.
- The fallback now runs after all exact and cross-suffix matches. So it cannot take a target that another source entry matches by name, whatever the source order.
- In real builds, the only output that changes is `LUT_B_MOE_ARCHS` on CUDA 13.4 without a 10.7 target. It goes from `10.0` to empty, so the kernel is skipped and LUT-B MoE uses its existing emulation path. Every other kernel's arch list and `CUDA_ARCHS` are unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** `tests/test_cmake_utils.py` adds two tests. Its CI step is currently disabled ("pending locked cmake installation"), so I ran it locally with cmake 4.4.4:

```
# this PR
$ pytest -q tests/test_cmake_utils.py -k "not hipify"
10 passed, 1 deselected

# the same tests with cmake/utils.cmake from main (86fdabec0)
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[cu134-release-list]        Expected '', got '10.0'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[lower-minor-arch-specific]  Expected '', got '10.0a'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[lower-minor-plain]          Expected '', got '12.0'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[skips-lower-minor]          Expected '10.7a', got '10.0a'
4 failed, 6 passed, 1 deselected
```

The hipify test is deselected because it needs torch. `test_family_arch_fallback_runs_after_name_matches` passes on main too. It guards the ordering: with only the version check and no separate fallback pass, `10.0f;10.7f` with targets `10.7a;10.3a` gives `10.7a` instead of `10.7a;10.3a`.

**Every call site.** I ran the old and new function with `cmake -P` on every `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` call. That covers 51 calls in `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/utils.cmake` and `cmake/external_projects/*.cmake`, with each CUDA-version branch. It also covers CUDA 11.8, 12.0, 12.3, 12.8, 12.9, 13.0 and 13.4, and every arch list the repo builds with: the release x86 and aarch64 lists, `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker-bake.hcl`, the CI image build scripts, and `.github/workflows/scripts/build.sh`. I applied the `CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` intersection first, as the build does. The only changed outputs were `LUT_B_MOE_ARCHS` on CUDA 13.4 (`10.0`, `10.0a` or `10.0f` → empty) and the existing test-only call in `tests/test_cmake_utils.py`.

**cu134 build image.** This ran in `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.4`, the cu134 release `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`, with torch `2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134`. With the release list, main configures `Building LUT-B MoE for archs: 10.0`, and that object fails with 103 ptxas errors such as `Instruction 'tcgen05.alloc' not supported on .target 'sm_100'`. I compared this version with the first version of this PR, the LUT-B-only filter. I configured both, then diffed every `... for archs` line and every command from `ninja -t commands`:

| `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` | `Building LUT-B MoE for archs:` | arch lines and compile commands vs first version | build |
|---|---|---|---|
| `7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0` (cu134 x86 release) | not printed | identical (577 commands) | `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` builds |
| `8.0 8.7 8.9 9.0 10.0 11.0 12.0` (aarch64 release list, configured in the x86 image) | not printed | identical (567 commands) | not run |
| `10.0 10.7` | `10.7f` | identical (544 commands) | LUT-B object builds with `arch=compute_107f,code=sm_107f` |

## Known limitations (unchanged by this PR)

I found these while reviewing the function. I left them out to keep this change small:

1. If the fallback target is plain, the plain value is emitted, so family features are off. For example, `10.0f` with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.7` on CUDA 13.4 gives plain `10.7`. Kernels whose list is only `10.0f` then compile for `compute_107` without family features, the same kind of failure as this bug. No release or CI list hits this. Emitting an `f` arch in that case would fix it.
2. Each source entry takes at most one target. For example, `10.0f` with targets `10.0a;10.7a` gives only `10.0a`.
3. "Same major, minor >= y" approximates the CUDA family table. With CUDA 12.x, 10.1 is not in the 10.0f family but still matches.
4. `+PTX` on an `f` source is dropped when it matches by cross-suffix or fallback.
5. The header comment of `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` still describes only the old `x.0a` special case.

## Details

**Why not a duplicate.** #66014 adds the same LUT-B-only filter as the first version of this PR. This PR instead fixes the shared arch selection, as maintainers suggested. The LUT-B result is the same, and the same mistake is prevented for other `f` sources.

**AI assistance.** I used Claude Code for the analysis, the change, the call-site comparison and the validation scripts. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` return `usage.prompt_tokens: 0` when the request omits `prompt_tokens`, because they never read the generate response's `usage`. They now fall back to the generate response's `usage.prompt_tokens`, as the streaming paths already do. Fixes #64778

## Claims

- Non-streaming chat derender without `prompt_tokens` returns the generate response's `usage.prompt_tokens` (10) instead of 0.
- Non-streaming completions derender without `prompt_tokens` returns the sum of the generate responses' `usage.prompt_tokens` (1 + 5 = 6) instead of 0.
- No change for requests that set `prompt_tokens`, 0 included.

## Validation

Both derender test files, with this PR cherry-picked onto main `349b21487a` (2026-11-04); the xfail is the existing `triples` case:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

`224 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 469.94s (0:07:49)`

```
XFAIL tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_matches_batch_reasoning[triples] - <think> leaks into reasoning when it shares a multi-token delta with reasoning text (vllm#55195)
224 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 469.94s (0:07:49)
```

</details>

Not tested: encoder-decoder and multimodal prompts, where the generate count includes encoder tokens; no such model was run.
Not tested: `test_derender_parity.py`, which starts a GPU server; no GPU was free.
No model eval: the change only sets the `usage` field of the derender response; token IDs and text are untouched.
The new tests run in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server` CI step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `ServingDerender.derender_chat_response` sets `prompt_tokens` to `request.prompt_tokens`, else 0, and `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion` expands an omitted list to `[0] * n`. Neither reads the generate response's `usage`, which `/inference/v1/generate` sets on every non-streaming response. The `prompt_tokens` docstrings on `DerenderChatRequest` and `DerenderCompletionRequest` documented the 0.

**Fix.** New `resolve_prompt_tokens(prompt_tokens, usage)` returns the request value if set (0 included), else `usage.prompt_tokens`, else 0 when `usage` is absent, the order `derender_chat_stream`, `_derender_chat_stream_parsed` and `derender_completion_stream` already used inline. All five sites call it, completions once per generate response, and the two docstrings, which `derenderer.md` includes, state this order; the stream sites' `or 0` is dropped because `UsageInfo.prompt_tokens` is a non-optional `int`.

**Related PRs.**

- #64041 — adds `reasoning_tokens` and `cached_tokens` to chat derender usage. It edits the `UsageInfo` in `derender_chat_response` next to this change and keeps the `else 0`; the two merge cleanly.
- #43606 — added the `/derender` endpoints. It introduced the `else 0`, the `[0] * n` default and the "defaults to 0 if omitted" docstrings this PR changes.
- #47301 — added streaming derender. It introduced the request-then-generate-usage order that `resolve_prompt_tokens` copies.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Give Mamba-1 LoRA layers every row of the batch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61853. With LoRA enabled, `MambaMixer` (Mamba-1, used by `JambaForCausalLM` and `MambaForCausalLM`) gave `x_proj`, `dt_proj` and `out_proj` only part of the batch's rows. The LoRA kernels index rows through the whole batch's mapping, so they went out of bounds. This PR gives those layers a batch-sized input when LoRA is enabled. Root cause and GPU traces: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61853#issuecomment-6516409227

## Claims

- `ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-dev` with `enable_lora=True` starts under the default configuration (MRV2, CUDA graphs) instead of hitting an illegal memory access during CUDA graph capture.
- A LoRA request on Jamba no longer crashes, or silently changes another request's output, when its batch mixes prefill and decode rows.
- No change when LoRA is disabled: that code path is untouched.

## Validation

A40 (SM86), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`. `mamba_mixer.py` did not change between that commit and this branch's base. "This PR" means the nightly with this diff applied.

The first commit also added `tests/lora/test_jamba.py`, which was removed at review. It built a seeded random adapter on the Mamba projections and compared a request alone against the same request decoding next to another request's prefill chunks (`check_logprobs_close`).
```
$ python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py            # main + the test
E           vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
(EngineCore pid=13570) ERROR 10-30 05:26:53 [core.py:1634] RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
======================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 50.83s =========================

$ python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py            # this PR
======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 29.28s ========================

$ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py   # this PR
======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 56.72s ========================
```

The issue's script (`LLM(model="ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-dev", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=32, max_model_len=4096, seed=42, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85)`, then one greedy `generate`):

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (MRV2, CUDA graphs) | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `max_lora_rank=64` | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `lora_target_modules=in_proj,x_proj,dt_proj,out_proj` | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `enable_lora=False` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |

Mixed prefill/decode batch: the random adapter, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`, a short request, and a ~2K-token request that prefills in chunks while the short one decodes. "short"/"long" compare each request's tokens in that run against the same request run alone:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| eager, MRV2 | illegal memory access | short same; long differs at one token |
| eager, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | illegal memory access | short same; long differs at one token |
| CUDA graphs, MRV2 | illegal memory access (the failing test run above) | short same, long same |
| CUDA graphs, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | short same, long differs | short same, long same |
| eager, MRV2, `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on `_lora_` kernels | `ERROR SUMMARY: 672 errors` (`Invalid __global__ read` in `_lora_expand_kernel`) | `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors` |

On main with CUDA graphs and MRV1, the long request alone gives `' Item 300 is a number. Item 2-30 is a number. ...'`. With this PR, every run gives `' Item 200 is a number. Item 200 is a number. Item 200 is a number. Item 201 is a number. ...'`. The one-token difference in eager mode is in the long request's alone run (`210` where every other run has `201`). It is the same under both runners, and the mixed run matches the CUDA graph runs, so I read it as batch-shape numerics rather than this bug.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `forward_impl` calls `_ssm_transform` once on the decode rows and once on the prefill rows, so `x_proj` and `dt_proj` each see part of the batch, and `out_proj` sees `num_actual_tokens` rows, without CUDA graph padding. The punica kernels take `token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids[:x.size(0)]` from `LoRAKernelMeta.meta_args`. Those are row ids of the whole batch sorted by LoRA id, so with fewer rows than the batch the expand kernel loads and stores output rows past the end. `cuda-gdb` on the capture-time core dump stops at `kernel_utils.py:231 tiled_out = tl.load(c_ptr, mask=c_mask)` in `_lora_expand_kernel`. `in_proj` already gets the full `hidden_states`. Mamba-2's `in_proj` and `out_proj` do too.

**Change.** Only when `is_lora_enabled`:
- `_ssm_transform` zero-pads its input to `hidden_states.shape[0]` rows, with the part at its batch offset (decode rows first, then prefill), runs `x_proj`/`dt_proj`, and slices the rows back.
- `out_proj` gets its input padded to `hidden_states.shape[0]` rows and keeps the first `num_actual_tokens`.

The padded copy also replaces the `.contiguous()` calls the LoRA path had. In a mixed batch, `x_proj` and `dt_proj` now run twice over the batch's rows instead of once per part. Both are small (1024→64 and 32→1024 on Jamba-tiny-dev), and only the LoRA path pays this. Slicing uses the metadata's Python ints, so there are no new host syncs.

**Tests.** No new test, per review. No test in `tests/lora` runs a Mamba-1 model, so CI does not cover this path.

**Not a duplicate.** #62553 also targets #61853. It restricts Jamba's LoRA modules to `qkv_proj, o_proj, gate_up_proj, down_proj, in_proj, embed_tokens, lm_head` and attributes the crash to MoE expert LoRA. LoRA on `experts` alone starts fine, and the crash comes from `x_proj`/`dt_proj`. That list avoids the crash by removing LoRA from those layers, and it does not cover `MambaForCausalLM`. This PR keeps LoRA on all of Jamba's modules. I searched open PRs for #61853, `mamba_mixer` + LoRA, and Jamba LoRA.

**Limitations.** Tested on Ampere (SM86) with Jamba-tiny-dev only. `MambaForCausalLM` shares the code path but I did not run a Mamba checkpoint with LoRA. Not tested with TP > 1 or on ROCm.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to trace the fault, write the change and the test, and run the GPU validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Handle leading missing packed groups
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix packed LoRA expansion when a multi-slice packed projection has a missing
leading member.

Qwen3.5 maps the two adapter-visible modules `in_proj_qkv` and `in_proj_z`
onto the four output slices Q, K, V, and Z. A valid PEFT adapter that targets
only `in_proj_z` is loaded as `[None, z_lora]`. The current implementation
assumes that a missing member covers every remaining output slice, so the
leading `None` consumes Q/K/V/Z and the subsequent Z tensor cannot be placed.

This is the converse of the trailing-`None` case fixed by #47640.

## Fix

A missing member's row count is unknown, so its coverage is inferred from the
present groups around it: groups before the first `None` are aligned from the
front, groups after the last `None` are aligned from the back, and the `None`
groups in between take the remaining slices (left at base weights).

Existing trailing-`None` and all-`None` behavior is preserved. Present B tensors
whose row counts don't match the output sizes, or present groups sandwiched
between missing ones, fail explicitly instead of silently misaligning weights.

## Reproduction

A real on-disk PEFT adapter was created for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` with only the
first GDN layer's `in_proj_z` targeted. Its files were a standard
`adapter_config.json` and `adapter_model.safetensors`, with rank 8 tensors:

```text
in_proj_z.lora_A.weight: [8, 1024]
in_proj_z.lora_B.weight: [2048, 8]
```

On the unmodified base commit, the first LoRA request terminates EngineCore:

```text
ValueError: Cannot determine how to split lora_b with 2048 rows into 4
slices with output sizes [2048, 2048, 2048, 2048] starting from index 4.
```

With this change, the same model, adapter, and request load successfully and
complete generation on Intel XPU.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py \
  -k 'column_parallel_packed or expand_packed_lora_with_missing_group' -q
python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -q
pre-commit run
```

The regression test covers `[valid, valid]`, `[valid, None]`,
`[None, valid]`, and `[None, None]`, and verifies the actual contents of every stacked A/B buffer.

## Test Result

- Focused packed-layer tests: 40 passed, 36 skipped.
- LoRA layer and manager suites: 248 passed, 182 skipped.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Real Qwen3.5 disk PEFT adapter: failed before the fix with the error above;
  loaded and generated successfully after the fix.
- A full `pre-commit run --all-files` additionally exposed an unrelated
  container-specific failure in `test-nonroot-entrypoint` case 3; all other
