commits.pr_title: [Perf][GDN] Fuse prefill state gather/scatter with the shared Triton kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replace eager GDN prefill state gather/scatter with the existing shared Triton `gather_initial_states` / `scatter_states` kernels for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 linear attention and Kimi KDA. Supersedes [#64498](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64498); see comparison below with [#50372](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50372). (Replaces #66058, which a branch rename auto-closed.)

## Claims

- Reduce prefill state gather/scatter from 4–5 eager kernels per layer per batch to one bandwidth-bound kernel per direction, covering every GDN prefill backend. Decode is unchanged.
- Improve the measured per-layer full prefill chain by 1.16–1.50x on a B300 GPU; isolated gather/scatter improves 4–30x.
- Preserve bitwise parity with the eager ops, including fresh-row zeroing and mixed-dtype scatter.

## Validation

Microbenchmarks on a B300 GPU: FlashInfer CUPTI timing, cold L2, CUDA-graph replayed chains, alternating arm order, medians of 5 rounds. Outputs are bitwise equal.

Per-layer full prefill chain (state gather/scatter + FlashInfer chunk kernel + write-back), fp32 pool, Qwen3.5-0.8B GDN dimensions. `B` is sequence count, `T` is tokens per sequence; mode is initial-state availability (`none`, `all`, or `mixed`).

| case | mode | main (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B=1 T=8192 | none | 139.5 | 119.6 | 1.17x |
| B=1 T=8192 | all | 139.2 | 119.7 | 1.16x |
| B=1 T=8192 | mixed | 138.8 | 120.2 | 1.16x |
| B=4 T=2048 | none | 93.2 | 75.4 | 1.24x |
| B=4 T=2048 | all | 93.2 | 77.0 | 1.21x |
| B=4 T=2048 | mixed | 93.3 | 76.5 | 1.22x |
| B=16 T=512 | none | 107.3 | 71.4 | 1.50x |
| B=16 T=512 | all | 107.3 | 74.5 | 1.43x |
| B=16 T=512 | mixed | 106.8 | 73.3 | 1.46x |

Isolated gather/scatter, same methodology: eager 83–714 µs versus fused 3.8–140 µs per layer across B=1..256 and fp32/bf16 pools (4–30x). At B=4 with an fp32 pool, eager gather takes 20.8 µs and bool-mask fill 32.0 µs; the fp32 cast is a no-op.

E2E forward benchmark: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, dummy weights, seeded, jitter 0; 2 alternating runs per arm, medians of each run's samples below (run-to-run spread <0.1% on every case):

| case (forward) | main (µs) | PR (µs) | delta |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| prefill 8192 | 11777.2 | 11461.8 | −2.7% |
| chunked prefill 2048@10240 | 4641.0 | 4355.8 | −6.1% |
| mix (64 decode + 4096 fresh prefill) | 8757.9 | 8436.8 | −3.7% |
| mixed-context prefill (2048 fresh + 2048 continuation) | 6936.3 | 6705.9 | −3.3% |
| decode 256×1@8192 | 6405.1 | 6409.2 | ~0 |

For reference, the closed pool-route PR measured −2.7% / −7.6% / −4.9% on the first three cases with the same tool; this PR is within ~1.5 points of it there, and additionally speeds up mixed fresh/cached batches, which the pool route could not.

E2E reproduction command:

```bash
vllm bench forward --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --kv-len-jitter 0 --seed 0 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --case prefill=8192 --case chunked=2048@10240c --case mix=64*1@8192,4096 \
  --case mixcached=2048,2048@8192c --case decode=256*1@8192
```

Tests run with the swaps in place:

- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gather_scatter_states.py`: **40 passed** on a B300 GPU. Absorbs the gather test previously in `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py` (subsumed by the parametrized matrix). Covers 2 pool dtypes × B in {1, 3, 64, 256} × contiguous/strided indices, padded pool row strides, and mixed-dtype scatter; assertions are bitwise against eager operations.
- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **78 passed**.
- CI: the H200-MIG mamba step collects `tests/kernels/mamba` by directory and already depends on the touched sources. The extended `tests/model_executor/test_qwen_triton_warmup.py` runs on the AMD Model Executor step (its deps cover `vllm/model_executor/warmup/` and `tests/model_executor`); the NVIDIA Model Executor step is disabled on main and returns with #65145. The JIT-monitor e2e step depends on `vllm/model_executor/warmup/` and fails on any post-warmup in-serving compile.

## Details

Eager prefill gathers `ssm[idx]`, zeros fresh rows through bool-mask `index_put`, casts, and scatters final states back into the cache pool. These 4–5 kernels per layer per batch run far below the bandwidth roofline. The replacement kernels already exist under `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, introduced with Kimi K3 KDA. They perform pure copies with cast-on-store only; bitwise parity with the eager operations follows from the copy semantics and is asserted in tests.

- **Qwen:** replace both gather sites (FlashInfer and non-FlashInfer `_forward_core`) and the shared scatter site. Extend the JIT-monitor-driven `qwen_triton_warmup` startup pass to compile both kernels for the variants serving reaches: fp32 (FlashInfer/FLA) and pool-dtype (CuteDSL/AITER) scatter sources, the unaligned index/mask pointers that mixed-batch slicing at `num_decodes` produces (Triton specializes on 16-byte pointer alignment), and strided index views from spec-decode block tables.
- **Kimi:** retain the existing fused gather and replace eager scatter. Register `scatter_states.register_warmup` at initialization, following glm5next. Add optional `src_dtype` to the scatter warmup spec for fp32 final states written into a bf16 pool.
- **XPU:** allow `scatter_states` on XPU, matching gather; the XPU Triton path reaches `_forward_core`.

Prior approaches: [#64498](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64498) (closed) routed through the pool, eliminating this gather/scatter only for homogeneous batches and coupling to FlashInfer's `state_indices` semantics. [#50372](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50372) (open, stalled) fuses the same gather/scatter with a 1-D div/mod indexing kernel limited to the FlashInfer path. This PR reuses kernels already in the tree and covers every GDN prefill backend.

Limitations: kernels retain their shipped configuration without further tuning. Measurements are on B300 (SM103); ROCm was not re-measured, though these kernels already run there through KDA.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Handle media cache eviction during reads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A media cache entry evicted between its metadata check and read can be recreated as an empty file, causing image decoding to fail. Treat this race as a cache miss so the media is downloaded again.

## Claims

- Refresh cache entry timestamps without recreating files removed by concurrent LRU eviction.
- Add synchronous and asynchronous regression coverage for cache eviction during reads.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py -q --tb=short`: 84 passed.
- The synchronous and asynchronous regression tests fail on the original implementation with an image-decoding error and pass with the fix.
- On a DGX Spark, a Qwen3.8-27B `LLM.chat` request reproduced the failure with the original cache method and succeeded with the patched method. Normal requests had identical prompt and generated token IDs. This test used installed vLLM 0.31.0 with the patched `_get_cached_bytes` method from this checkout injected into the runtime.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md`: passed.

## Details

`Path.touch()` recreates a cache file if eviction occurs after `stat()`. The resulting empty file is returned as a cache hit, so image decoding fails instead of fetching the media again. `os.utime()` updates the timestamp only when the file exists; if eviction wins the race, the existing `OSError` handler returns a cache miss.

This change addresses the read/eviction race. It does not repair already-corrupt cache files or measure production incidence. It is separate from [#56062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56062), which bounds cache entries and handles failed downloads, and [#55616](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55616), which changes cache lookup identity.

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Match default MM LoRA for OpenAI input_audio parts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Default per-modality LoRAs (`--default-mm-loras`, e.g. `{"audio": "<path>"}`)
are auto-selected by matching the LoRA name against the modalities present in a
chat request. `BaseServing._get_message_types` derives each content part's
modality with `type.split("_")[0]`:

- `audio_url` → `audio` ✅
- `image_url` → `image` ✅
- `input_audio` → `input` ❌ (should be `audio`)

`input_audio` is a fully supported OpenAI chat content type and maps to the
`audio` modality during parsing (`vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py`,
`part_type == "input_audio"` → `modality = "audio"`). Because the modality is
mis-derived as `input`, an `audio` default LoRA **never activates** for requests
that send audio via `input_audio`.

## Fix

Map OpenAI-style `input_<modality>` parts to `<modality>` (so `input_audio` →
`audio`), keeping the existing `<modality>_url` → `<modality>` behavior.

## Reproduction

Calling the real `_get_message_types` on a chat request:

Before:
```
audio_url   -> {'audio'}
input_audio -> {'input'}     # audio default LoRA never matches
```

After:
```
audio_url   -> {'audio'}
input_audio -> {'audio'}
```

## Verification

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_serving_models.py -k message_types -v
...
tests/.../test_get_message_types_maps_audio_parts_to_audio[audio_url-part0] PASSED
tests/.../test_get_message_types_maps_audio_parts_to_audio[input_audio-part1] PASSED
2 passed
```

Lint/type checks (pre-commit): `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy-3.10`, SPDX — all
pass on the changed files.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR on `vllm-project/vllm` targets default-MM-LoRA modality
detection / `_get_message_types` for `input_audio` (the feature was added in
#19126 and has not been touched since).

## Scope

One bug, one root cause: a 10-line change in `_get_message_types` plus a single
parametrized regression test. No behavior change for existing `*_url` / `text`
parts.

---

AI assistance was used to help identify, reproduce, and fix this bug; the change
has been reviewed and verified locally.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen3-Omni] Size the video encoder budget from the processor's video limits
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen3-Omni sizes its video encoder budget from the image limits (3584x3584 frames), but the HF processor caps video frames at `768 * 32 * 32` pixels. The budget therefore stops short of `max_model_len`, and valid video requests are rejected with HTTP 400, for example a 60 s 896x504 clip at 2 fps with `--max-model-len 32768`. The same mismatch makes startup profiling run the vision encoder on a dummy video of ~1.5k tokens instead of a long one. This sizes both from the processor's video limits. Clef-Omni shares the code and caps frames lower (`MAX_FRAME_PIXELS`), so it gets its own canvas.

## Claims

- Fixes the erroneous encoder-budget rejection of valid video requests within the context limit. The 60 s clip above returns 200 instead of `video item with 26880 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 25088`, and a 145 s clip at `--max-model-len 65536` (64,960 video tokens, budget 62,720 on main) also returns 200. Clef-Omni at 32k has the same gap: a 120 s 896x504 clip is 30,240 video tokens against a 25,088 budget on main, and fits the 32,768 budget with this PR (checked on the processor, not served).
- On main there is no setting that raises the budget short of `--max-num-batched-tokens`: `--limit-mm-per-prompt` video options only shrink the profiling dummy (`_get_dummy_videos` ignores larger values), and the budget stays 25,088 with them.
- Startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a video that fills the budget: 32,256 / 65,280 video tokens at `max_model_len` 32768 / 65536 for Qwen3-Omni (1,458 / 3,645 on main), and 32,768 at 32k for Clef-Omni (512 on main).
- It also closes an engine crash on main. On an H100 80GB at the default `max_model_len` (65,536), main starts, but a 120 s clip it admits (55,339 tokens) runs the vision encoder out of memory (`torch.OutOfMemoryError` in the vision MLP), and every request after that returns 500. With this PR, startup reports that the KV cache only fits 20,816 tokens and asks for a lower `--max-model-len`, instead of failing under load.
- Images are unchanged (budget 12,544, same dummy).
- Trade-off: profiling a full-length video reserves more memory, so the KV cache is smaller: -3.0 GiB at 32k and -7.6 GiB at 65k on an H200 (below). On an 80 GB H100 this means the default 65k context no longer starts (see the crash above for what main does there). This is the reservation Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL already make: at 32k their processed profiling video is 100% of the video budget (32,768 and 12,288 tokens), while Qwen3-Omni's was 6% (1,458 of 25,088).

## Validation

New tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py` use the real processors: the budget reaches `max_model_len`, a 30 s 896x504 clip (13,440 video tokens) fits it at 16k, the profiling dummy fills the budget within one temporal step for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni, the video canvas matches what processing produces (no override, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`, and Clef-Omni's cap), and the image budget is unchanged.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py   # 16 passed (12 new)
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_audio_in_video.py   # 40 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "Qwen3-Omni or clef"   # 10 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passes
```

With both model files from main, 11 of the 12 new tests fail (the image test passes on both). With only `clef_omni.py` from main, the 3 Clef-Omni cases fail:

```
E   assert 25088 == 32768
E   assert 12544 == 16384
E   assert (12544 - 768) < 729
E   assert (12544 - 768) < 256
E   AttributeError: 'Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo' object has no attribute 'get_video_size_with_most_features'
11 failed, 5 passed
```

End to end on an H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`, the same wheel with only the model file swapped, `vllm serve` with the default `--max-num-batched-tokens` and `--media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": -1, "fps": 2}}'`:

| `--max-model-len` | request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32768 | 60 s 896x504 clip, `use_audio_in_video` (27,680 tokens) | 400 | 200 |
| 65536 | same 60 s clip | 200 | 200, same greedy text |
| 65536 | 145 s 896x504 clip, video only (64,977 tokens) | 400 | 200 |
| 65536 | 4 concurrent 120 s clips with audio (55,339 tokens each) | 200 | 200 |

| `--max-model-len` | encoder budget main → PR | KV cache memory main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 32768 | 25,088 → 32,768 | 64.13 → 61.11 GiB |
| 65536 | 62,720 → 65,536 | 64.11 → 56.47 GiB |

The 60 s request returned identical greedy text on main and with this PR. The four concurrent requests had equal prompt-token counts on both; 2 of the 4 outputs match and the other 2 diverge after about ten words, for a reason I haven't confirmed (vLLM is not batch invariant by default). The maximum sampled GPU memory across the 65k request phase was 141,461 MiB on main and 136,251 MiB with this PR (of 143,771 MiB). These serving runs used the revision before the switch to `_merge_kwargs`, which resolves the same video size (checked with no override, a scoped override and unrelated kwargs). `test_model_tensor_schema` passes for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni on main and with this PR on the same GPU.

The same check on an H100 80GB, default `--max-model-len` (65,536), with the same requests in order:

| | startup | 60 s clip | 120 s clip with audio (55,339 tokens) | 60 s clip again |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | starts, 9.53 GiB KV cache | 200 | 500, `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.72 GiB` in the vision encoder; engine dead | 500 |
| this PR | `ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (65536), (6.0 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (1.91 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 20816.` | | | |

## Details

- Root cause: `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo` inherits the Qwen2-VL video estimate, which uses the largest image (3584x3584, 12,544 tokens per two frames with patch size 16) and adds frames until `seq_len`. That stops at 25,088 for 32k. Processing then shrinks real frames to the processor's video default (`Qwen3OmniMoeProcessorKwargs` videos `size`, `longest_edge = 768 * 32 * 32`), which is also why the dummy video only reaches ~1.5k tokens.
- The video size now comes from where processing takes it: flat `size` / `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` over `video_processor.size` (as in #49015), otherwise the processor's merged `videos_kwargs`, resolved with `processor._merge_kwargs` as Gemma 3 does for its image size. Frames are added at that size until `seq_len`, without the 14-frame dummy cap, because this processor caps pixels per frame rather than per video, so a single video can fill the prompt. The per-item budget is therefore `seq_len`, the same pattern as #59565 sizing GLM-5.3 images from the exact token ceiling.
- `Qwen3OmniMoeProcessorKwargs` and its video defaults are the same in transformers 5.16.1 and 5.22.1, the range vLLM supports.
- #65534 (configurable `--encoder-cache-size`) is complementary: it changes cache capacity, while this fixes the per-item size that the cache is floored to.
- #63809 (Qwen3-Omni ViT CUDA graphs) reads `get_num_frames_with_most_features` for its `max_frames_per_video`, which sizes the `cu_seqlens` buffer. With this change it returns 84 frames at 32k instead of 4. That is the frame count of the profiling input at the largest frame size, not a bound on every valid video: smaller frames allow more.
- Qwen2.5-Omni has the same under-profiling (its processed profiling video is 1,458 of a 32,768 budget at 32k) but not the 400 at 32k, so I left it for a separate change.
- The shared Qwen2-VL estimate has the same gap whenever `max_model_len` is not a multiple of its two-frame step. With Qwen2.5-VL (step 16,384) at `--max-model-len 40000` the budget is 32,768, while a 68 s 896x504 clip is 39,168 tokens. I kept this PR to Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni, where the gap shows up at the common 32k setting, and can follow up on the shared estimate.

---

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix low draft acceptance with DeepSeek-V4 MTP under pipeline parallelism by sharing the target's input embedding with the drafter. This uses the existing embedding-sharing mechanism, as in [#58648](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58648).

## Claims

- Restores PP2 draft acceptance from 0.030 to 0.820, matching the PP1 baseline.
- Maintains comparable GSM8K accuracy: 0.949 with the fix versus 0.948 on main.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on B300, TP2 + EP, MegaMoE, MRV2, and MTP with 2 speculative tokens.

| Configuration | GSM8K accuracy | Draft acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| PP1, main | 0.947 | 0.820 |
| PP2, main | 0.948 | 0.030 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.949 | 0.820 |

GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot. Draft acceptance is total accepted tokens divided by total drafted tokens over the evaluation.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative_config.method=mtp \
  --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
```

Use `--pipeline-parallel-size 1` for the PP1 baseline.

`pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k may_use_target_embed`: **2 passed**. Without the fix, the DeepSeek-V4 case fails because `may_use_target_embed` is `False`; the OPT control passes in both versions.

## Details

The checkpoint contains no separate MTP embedding. Under PP, the NVIDIA `DeepSeekV4MTP` does not declare `has_own_embed_tokens`, so the target's last stage omits its embedding and `maybe_share_target_embed` returns early. The drafter uses an unloaded embedding, causing almost every draft token to be rejected.

Setting `has_own_embed_tokens = False` enables both parts of the existing mechanism: the registry marks the drafter as `may_use_target_embed`, causing the target's last PP stage to load the embedding, and the drafter then shares that module. The retained embedding is TP-sharded (0.49 GiB per GPU at TP2 in this setup).

The change and registry regression test cover the NVIDIA implementation. Related PRs address other models: [#63141](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63141) adds an error for DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 MTP, and [#62903](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62903) fixes Inkling MTP.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Read per-layer embeddings on later pipeline stages
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix corrupted output from Gemma 4 models with per-layer embeddings (PLE) under pipeline parallelism by loading the PLE tensor received from the preceding stage.

## Claims

- Restore PLE consumption on every pipeline stage in the shared Gemma 4 text and multimodal model implementation.
- Add a PP=2 versus PP=1 generation regression test for `google/gemma-4-E2B`.

## Validation

Run the regression test on two GPUs:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_per_layer_embeddings_pipeline_parallel
```

The test compares PP=1 and PP=2 using eight prompts, greedy decoding, 32 output tokens, and top-5 logprobs with `check_logprobs_close`. On 2× B300:

| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| Before fix | Failed: PP=2 generated corrupted text |
| With fix | Passed |

The `distributed(num_gpus=2)` marker includes the test in the existing Distributed Models CI suite.

Serving validation with `vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it` on B300, comparing PP=2 (`VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=13,22`) against PP=1:

| Version | Mean absolute prompt logprob difference | Maximum absolute difference | Prompt NLL | Generated text |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PP=1 reference | — | — | 6.885 | Reference |
| PP=2 before fix | 10.09 | 37.7 | 15.15 | Corrupted |
| PP=2 with fix | 0.071 | 0.62 | 6.879 | Matches reference |

An image-input check using `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` with a four-layer configuration and non-uniform dummy weights reduced the maximum PP=2 versus PP=1 prompt logprob difference from 2.06 to 0.0.

## Details

On stages after the first, `Gemma4Model.forward` receives PLE through `intermediate_tensors`, while its `per_layer_inputs` argument is `None`. The previous guard checked that argument and skipped loading the received tensor. The updated guard checks for the `per_layer_inputs` key in `intermediate_tensors.tensors`.

The test uses the base checkpoint to generate continuations from raw prompts. Its `13,22` pipeline partition places layers 13–34 together, keeping KV source layers 13 and 14 on the same stage as all 20 KV-shared layers.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Count prompts over max_model_len in Anthropic count_tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/messages/count_tokens` returns HTTP 400 ("This model's maximum context length is ...") for any conversation longer than `max_model_len`, so a client cannot learn how long such a conversation is, which is exactly when it needs the number to trim it. `/tokenize` counts the same messages. This makes `count_tokens` tokenize without the context-length check, as `/tokenize` does; generation requests keep the check.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages/count_tokens` returns `input_tokens` for a prompt longer than `max_model_len`, equal to the `/tokenize` count for the same messages, instead of a 400.
- Prompts within the limit are counted as before, equal to `usage.input_tokens` of the same `/v1/messages` request (also with a system prompt, tools or disabled thinking), and `/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` still reject over-length prompts.

## Validation

New test `test_count_tokens_over_max_model_len` in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py`, on the module's existing `RemoteOpenAIServer` (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--max-model-len 2048`). It counts a ~3,000-token conversation with the Anthropic SDK, compares the result with `/tokenize`, and checks that `messages.create` still rejects the same conversation.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py -k test_count_tokens_over_max_model_len
```

Before the fix (main at 7663a8c):

```
>       count = await client.messages.count_tokens(
E           anthropic.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'message': "This model's maximum context length is 2048 tokens. However, your prompt contains at least 2049 input tokens, which exceeds this limit even without any output tokens. ..."}}
1 failed
```

After the fix: `1 passed`. The test runs in the existing `entrypoints/anthropic` CI step.

Probe server: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3`. One user message of N repeated words, before (7663a8c) and after this change:

| Words | `/tokenize` count | `count_tokens` before | `count_tokens` after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 300 | 309 | 309 | 309 |
| 1900 | 1909 | 1909 | 1909 |
| 2100 | 2109 | 400 | 2109 |
| 4000 | 4009 | 400 | 4009 |
| 2100, plus one tool | — | 400 | 2248 |

Prompts that fit, compared with `usage.input_tokens` of a `/v1/messages` request with the same body (`max_tokens: 1`); identical before and after:

| Request | `count_tokens` | `/v1/messages` `input_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one short user message | 15 | 15 |
| + `system` | 24 | 24 |
| + one tool | 154 | 154 |
| + `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | 19 | 19 |

With the 2100-word message, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` return 400 ("maximum context length is 2048 tokens") both before and after.

Other checks after the fix:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py` (whole file) | 10 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/`: `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`, `test_error_type_mapping.py`, `test_protocol_exports.py` | 151 passed; 3 failed: the `TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_non_jinja_renderer[deepseek-ai/...]` cases need DeepSeek configs from the Hugging Face Hub, which this machine cannot reach, and fail the same way on main |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed (shellcheck skipped: no shell files) |

Environment: CPU only (Intel i5-11300H), Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2, Python 3.12, `--enforce-eager`. The Python sources are this branch; the compiled CPU extensions come from the nightly CPU wheel for dd4e401 (31 commits behind, with no CPU kernel or custom-op changes in between). No model evaluation: generation is unchanged.

## Details

- Root cause: `count_tokens` converts the request with `to_chat_completion_request` and renders it through `render_chat_request`, which tokenizes with `ChatCompletionRequest.build_tok_params` (`max_total_tokens=max_model_len`). Tokenization then stops at `max_model_len + 1` tokens and `_token_len_check` raises. `/tokenize` renders with `max_total_tokens=None`.
- Fix: `_build_base_request` already builds count requests separately (without sampling fields); it now builds them as `_CountTokensChatRequest`, a `ChatCompletionRequest` whose `build_tok_params` matches `TokenizeChatRequest.build_tok_params` (`max_total_tokens=None`, `max_output_tokens=0`). That turns off both the length check and the early truncation, for counting only. `count_tokens` still renders through `render_chat_request`, so templating, tools, thinking and the tool/reasoning parsers are the same as for `/v1/messages`; no shared signatures change.
- Harmony (gpt-oss) chat rendering does not apply tokenization params, so `count_tokens` already counted over-length prompts there; unchanged.
- Counting an over-length prompt now tokenizes all of it, the same work `/tokenize` already does for such a prompt; generation paths are unchanged.
- Why count rather than reject: Anthropic presents token counting as the way to check that a prompt fits the context window before sending it ("Use token counts to ... fit prompts to a target length", [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting)), and an error that says "at least 2049" does not tell the client how much to trim. #64050 (open) adds an OpenAI Responses `input_tokens` endpoint that mirrors the generation request's validation; this PR does not touch it.

Not a duplicate: searched open and closed issues and PRs for `count_tokens` (by title: #63573/#61063 tool-parser requirement, #59180 thinking and `output_config`, #52896/#47753 Rust frontend, #44725 load counter, #35588 the original endpoint), "count_tokens max_model_len", "count_tokens maximum context length" and "count tokens context length". #59616/#59617 (open) change `/v1/messages` context-overflow errors and stop reasons, not counting.

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used to find the bug, write the change and test, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Handle EOS in speculative Guidance batches
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix Guidance rejecting committed speculative token batches that contain EOS followed by more tokens when `ignore_eos=True`.

## Claims

- Validate the grammar only through the first primary EOS, preserving the caller's generated token list.
- Keep invalid-prefix rejection atomic and preserve normal EOS stopping and speculative rollback.

## Validation

CPU, PR head `055ccc9fb` plus the test correction: **81 passed, 2 existing xfails** across the Guidance, grammar-backend and structured-output-manager suites. The two new regression cases fail on the unmodified base. Changed-file pre-commit passes, including mypy and CI selection.

H200 ×1, OPT-125M, using the CI image built from `055ccc9fb`: the revised regression test fails with the unpatched backend—grammar rejection stops generation after 5 of 8 tokens—and passes with the fix, producing all eight tokens with a length finish reason and nonzero speculative acceptance. The test forces the `a → EOS` prefix through grammar masking and allowed token IDs, without the unsupported `logit_bias` setting.

GPU, vLLM 0.32.0 with the equivalent fix backported: H200 ×8 / TP8, Mistral Medium 3.5 FP8 with its [EAGLE draft](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-EAGLE), k=3, context 262144, concurrency 8, `ignore_eos=True`. Actual request payloads were identical between runs.

| Streaming check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed requests | 10/16 | 16/16 |
| Grammar-related SSE500 errors | 6 | 0 |
| Exact requested output lengths | 10/10 successful requests | 16/16; 41,660 output tokens |

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q

# H200, from the repository root:
pytest -v -s \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py::test_guidance_ignore_eos_with_speculative_decoding

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py
```

</details>

## Details

Guidance already accepts further tokens after grammar termination. However, it rejects a batch containing EOS and a suffix before checking that state. The same tokens can therefore succeed one at a time and fail when committed together. The older bulk-consumption implementation can also leave the matcher in an invalid state after consuming past EOS.

Pass only the prefix through EOS to the matcher. The existing atomic acceptance and rollback from [#61557](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61557) remain intact. Normal EOS stopping trims the generated batch before grammar acceptance; temporary draft-mask advancement uses singleton tokens.

Related open [#65608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65608) handles additional request/model stop tokens. This change concerns the tokenizer's primary EOS and does not add stop-token mapping. When combining the changes, primary-EOS prefix handling should precede additional-stop mapping.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Add the bias in the SM120 NVFP4 CUTLASS GEMM epilogue
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

NVFP4 linears add the bias in a separate kernel after the GEMM. When the output goes straight to the attention custom op (the QKV projection of BERT/XLM-R and Qwen2-style models), Inductor cannot fuse that add, and on large prefills it costs more than the GEMM. This PR adds an optional `bias` to `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm`, applied in the SM120 epilogue (CUTLASS `LinCombPerColBias`) as the FP8 CUTLASS path already does, and passes it from `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`.

## Claims

- The SM120 epilogue add costs 0.007 ms on an 81920 x 3072 x 1024 GEMM, vs 0.749 ms for a separate `out + bias`.
- `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` passes the bias to the GEMM on SM12x unless N is padded.
- `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 with `linear_backend="cutlass"`: 12-13% less GPU time per batch on an RTX PRO 6000.

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`: 28 passed, 14 of them with a bias.

bge-reranker-v2-m3 (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, classifier excluded), `linear_backend="cutlass"`, GPU kernel time of one `classify` call on 128 sequences; two alternating rounds per arm agree within 0.1 ms:

| | 128 x 640 tokens | 128 x 320 tokens |
|---|---|---|
| main (separate bias add) | 135.1 ms | 60.4 ms |
| this PR | **119.1 ms** | **52.5 ms** |

The QKV bias kernels (16.1 ms at 640 tokens) disappear and the GEMMs take 0.4 ms longer; Inductor already fuses the other bias adds into the next LayerNorm or GELU kernel. Recall@10 on 60 questions each of Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko: 0.898 / 0.941 vs 0.881 / 0.950 (one question or less either way); mean |logit − FP32| 0.675 / 0.702 vs 0.676 / 0.695.

<details>
<summary>GEMM microbenchmark and commands</summary>

bge-reranker-v2-m3 GEMMs at 128 x 640 tokens, FP16 output:

| M x N x K | GEMM | GEMM + bias epilogue | `out + bias` alone | max diff vs separate add |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 81920 x 3072 x 1024 (QKV) | 0.447 ms | 0.454 ms | 0.749 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 1024 x 1024 (attn out) | 0.163 ms | 0.164 ms | 0.265 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 4096 x 1024 (FFN up) | 0.593 ms | 0.599 ms | 0.991 ms | 0.0039 |
| 81920 x 1024 x 4096 (FFN down) | 0.476 ms | 0.478 ms | 0.265 ms | 0.0078 |

The difference is one FP16 rounding of the GEMM output before the add.

```python
# GEMM: median of flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, cold_l2_cache=True, use_cuda_graph=True) for
#   fn = lambda: ops.cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm(x_fp4, w_fp4, x_sf, w_sf, alpha, torch.float16, bias=bias)  # or bias=None
#   fn = lambda: out + bias

# Model: VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1, prefix caching off. The main arm runs this branch with
# bias_epilogue forced to False in CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel, which is main's code path.
llm = LLM(nvfp4_checkpoint, runner="pooling", dtype="float16", linear_backend="cutlass")
# torch.profiler around one llm.classify call on 128 prompts; sum of CUDA kernel time
```

</details>

## Details

**Kernel.** `Fp4GemmSm120` gets a `HasBias` template flag that switches the epilogue from `LinearCombination` to `LinCombPerColBias` (D = alpha * acc + bias[n]); the dispatch instantiates both and picks one by whether a bias is passed.

**Default backend.** SM120 selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` first, and FlashInfer's `mm_fp4` takes no bias (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2290, closed as not planned), so this helps where `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` is selected. On bge both backends' GEMMs take about the same time, so `cutlass` becomes the faster choice there; the default stays because FlashInfer's autotuned GEMM is faster on Qwen3-4B decode shapes.

**Limitations.** SM100 is unchanged because I could not test it: its kernel rejects a bias, and the linear keeps the separate add there. CI has no SM12x runner, so the bias test cases are skipped in CI.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR adds a bias to `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm` or to the NVFP4 linear kernels.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which wrote the change and tests, ran the validation above and drafted this description.

commits.pr_title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by unresolved autorefs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The strict MkDocs build (Read the Docs, `fail_on_warning: true`) has been failing on `main` since 2026-11-05 with `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`. Every PR's docs check fails with the same warnings, e.g. builds [35688234](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688234/) (`main` at `e336407a3d`) and [35688313](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688313/). This PR fixes the docstrings behind those warnings. No code behavior changes.

## Claims

- The strict docs build passes again. All 12 `mkdocs_autorefs: Could not find cross-reference target` warnings are gone.
- The only changes are docstrings. No code changes.

## Validation

Ran the same command as Read the Docs, with `requirements/docs.txt` installed in a clean venv:

```bash
uv venv -p 3.12 /tmp/docs-venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/docs-venv uv pip install -r requirements/docs.txt
/tmp/docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --site-dir /tmp/docs-site --config-file mkdocs.yaml --strict
```

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`e336407a3d`) | Exit 1, `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`, the same 12 warnings as Read the Docs build 35688234 |
| This PR | Exit 0, `Documentation built in 178.18 seconds`, no warnings |

## Details

There are two root causes.

**1. MiniMax-M3.1 drafter docstrings (11 warnings), from #65386.**
- Some docstrings write array shapes as consecutive brackets, such as `red[8 t + wave][row][token]`, `x [16][K]`, `x_in [rows][6144]`, `x8[t][16 tid ..]`, `xs8[t][tid / 2]` and `o [112][128]`.
- Markdown parses `[a][b]` as a reference-style link, so autorefs tries to resolve `b` (`row`, `K`, `6144`, `16 tid ..`, `tid / 2`, `128`) and fails.
- Fix: wrap these shapes in code spans in `drafter/device.py` (`red_store`, `xq_chunk`, `row_x`, `quant_store`) and `drafter/attention.py` (`store_partial`). Single brackets such as `[1, rank, site]` are not affected, so they are left as is.

**2. `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` lost its docstring (1 warning), from #54109.**
- #54109 renamed the documented class to `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModularBase`, then added new `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular` subclasses without docstrings.
- mkdocstrings skips objects without a docstring by default, so the API page has no anchor for `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. The link in `docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md` then cannot resolve.
- Fix: give both subclasses a one-line docstring that names their activation quantization, so both get API anchors. The docs link stays as it is, because it names the concrete experts class.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: reset MoE expert padding at begin
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

At the start of a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336), zero MoE expert padding, so that post-load processing reruns over the same bytes as a cold start. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

MoE expert parameters are often larger than the checkpoint tensors loaded into them: DeepEP rounds the hidden size up, MXFP4 / TRT-LLM / AITER backends round the intermediate size, and block-aligned FP8 TP pads shards. Loaders copy only the checkpoint part. On a direct reload the padding then holds the previous post-processed bytes, which post-load processing processes again. After a `load_format=dummy` cold start (the usual RL setup) it holds random values.

## Claims

- **gpt-oss-20b (TP2, MXFP4), direct reload through IPC weight transfer:** every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh start, both after 3 same-weight syncs and after a dummy start plus one sync. On main, 168 expert tensors differ after every sync and drift from one sync to the next. After a dummy start, 288 differ and GSM8K drops about 2 points.
- Cold start and layerwise reload are unchanged.
- No loader changes: whether to fill is decided from `moe_config` when the checkpoint layout is recorded at cold start, so it also covers dummy and other cold starts that skip loaders, and the load plan (#64418) that bypasses them.

## Validation

**This PR's head (`1e25cc87e2`) with #66010 (`84ab98b6d8`) applied, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 1319 questions, 3 updates; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid). Differing expert parameters are 0 on every rank after every update. Jobs 45934, 45935.

| Sleep | Start | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 2 | Real | 0.9090 → 0.8984 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.8999 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| None | Real | 0.9007 → 0.8969 → 0.9022 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 |

**Layerwise reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise`, the default).** `materialize_meta_tensor` now zeroes the tensor it allocates, because loaders write only checkpoint regions and padding otherwise keeps uninitialized memory. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, no sleep, 1319 questions, on main `5c97556318` with and without that one line. Jobs 46042, 46043.

| Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 160 / 160 / 160 | 0.9037 → 0.0 → 0.0 |
| With the zero fill | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8954 → 0.9007 → 0.9030 |

`test_padded_moe_reload_releases_each_layer` fails 8 of 16 cases without the line.

**main vs this PR, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, reload from disk, no sleep mode; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with each arm's Python files overlaid, PR at e6403484fc; later commits change a comment and a CI trigger and merge main). "Differing" counts expert parameters per rank, out of 160, against a real cold start on the same arm. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. Jobs 45840, 45841.

| Start | Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real | main | 120 / 120 / 120 | 0.9052 → 0.9105 → 0.8984 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9014 → 0.9067 → 0.9075 |
| Dummy | main | 160 / 160 / 160 | — → 0.8787 → 0.8400 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | — → 0.8976 → 0.8999 |

On main after a dummy start the padding is random and GSM8K keeps falling across updates. Run-to-run noise on the real cold start is up to 1.5 points, so the real-start GSM8K rows don't separate the arms; the tensor counts do.

**Earlier revision.** The tables below ran before the fill became zero-only (it then kept block scales at 1).

**End to end** (GB200, nightly wheel 81a2879403 with each arm's Python files overlaid, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, real IPC weight transfer). "Differing" means device tensors (registered and reachable from module attributes) whose digest differs from a fresh real start; GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. The PR ran at 5b3856b564; later commits change only tests.

| Model (TP, MoE backend) | Arm | Real start + 3 syncs: differing | GSM8K | Dummy start + 1 sync: differing | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (TP2, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16`) | main | 168 / 168 / 168 | 0.9030 | 288 | 0.8825 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9022 | 0 | 0.8969 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, intermediate 576 → 640; NCCL, trainer on a second node) | main | 120 / 120 / 120 per rank | 0.9022 | 160 per rank (MoE)† | — |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9045 | 0 (MoE)† | — |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4, FlashInfer TRT-LLM, intermediate 192 → 256) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8961 | 0 | 0.8878 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8939 | 0 | 0.8961 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP4, Triton, block-aligned TP) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9075 | 1152* | 0.8992 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9037 | 1152* | 0.9007 |

- On main, the gpt-oss tensors that differ are expert biases and scales after real-start syncs, and all six expert parameters after a dummy start.
- The two Qwen3 configs are already correct on main: `_zero_intermediate_padding` and the block-aligned TP loader fill rewrite their padding on every load. They show the change does no harm.
- \* Attention KV-cache scales the checkpoint doesn't contain keep their random dummy values. This happens on both arms and isn't MoE padding; it's fixed separately (KV-scale `dummy_weight_value`).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: on main the 120 tensors per rank are `w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` of all 40 MoE layers, and their bytes change on every sync; after a dummy start `w2_weight` differs too. PR 3 ran at b5130fff61, main at e5d9bad98e. † The Engram embedding tables (about 203 GB, tensors of ~98 GB) can't be sent through the transfer path, so after a dummy start they keep dummy values in both arms and GSM8K isn't meaningful there; they are the only tensors that differ on this PR.
- Jobs: 44520, 44529 (gpt-oss); 44521 (BF16); 44522, 44530 (FP8); 45005, 45002 (DeepSeek-V4.1).

**Cold-start A/B** (A = main 81a2879403, B = this PR a096f3f138, same nightly wheel, same node, arms back to back). GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions; throughput from `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64.

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K A → B | Output tok/s A → B | KV cache A → B |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4, chat GSM8K (TP2) | 0.8886 → 0.8976 | 14390 → 14727 | 7.259M → 7.259M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4; intermediate 192 → 256) | 0.8946 → 0.8893 | 9230 → 9444 | 6.791M → 6.791M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (TP4) | 0.9045 → 0.9083 | 7269 → 7098 | 7.274M → 7.274M |

All within noise: GSM8K within 1 point, throughput within 2.4% in both directions, KV cache identical. At cold start this PR only records the fill list (jobs 44551–44553).

**Unit tests** (GB200, job 44519):
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py::test_direct_reload_after_dummy_start_resets_padding[block|static]` builds a real fp8 `RoutedExperts` with intermediate 256 → 384, fills every parameter with 7 instead of loading, records, then begins and loads. It checks that the result equals a zero-initialized load, that per-expert scalars and `e_score_correction_bias` are left alone, and that the record made at cold start decides the fill.
- `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` and `test_direct_reload.py` and `test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py` on the final code: 153 passed (GB200 job 23710). Earlier, `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` and `test_reload.py -k padded` (layerwise) also passed.

## Details

**Design.**
- `RoutedExperts.padding_fill_params()` applies when `moe_config` shows the hidden size or the per-partition intermediate size rounded up past its unpadded value, or block-aligned TP sharding.
- It returns the layer's parameters minus per-expert scalars: a parameter is filled if it has more than two values per expert. So per-tensor and static input scales, which may be absent from the checkpoint, are kept.
- `record_checkpoint_layout` stores `(module, name)` at cold start, before post-load processing. Some post-load processing pads only the runtime copy and writes the padded size back into `moe_config`, so the decision must not be made later.
- `begin_direct_reload` looks up each name after the view-back, skips parameters post-load processing has dropped, and zero-fills the rest whole. Loaders then overwrite every checkpoint region.

**Requirement.** The fill erases the checkpoint region too, so every checkpoint tensor loaded into these parameters must be resent on every update. The direct delivery contract in `direct.py` says so; the completeness check (F2 in #54477) will enforce it.

**Padding value.** Everything is filled with 0. A padding-only scale block only multiplies weights the same fill zeroes, so its value doesn't change the output. MXFP4 (DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss) and NVFP4 scales are created as zeros or empty, so 0 also matches a cold start. Block-aligned TP padding is rewritten by its loader after the fill, with scales at 1. Weights created with `torch.empty` had uninitialised padding at cold start; they get 0 here.

**`moe_config` is the source today, not the only possible one.** A layer padded some other way implements `padding_fill_params()` and reuses the same fill.

**Not changed.** Layerwise reload, the block-aligned TP loader fill, and `_zero_intermediate_padding` (cold start still needs it, since those weights are `torch.empty`).

**History.** This replaces this PR's earlier design, where loaders recorded the padding regions on every load and `fill_padding` wrote them before post-load processing. That design worked with layerwise reload and partial updates. Under the decision to require full updates and to drop layerwise reload (#54477), the fill at begin is much smaller and needs no loader changes. The streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 TP split moved to #65353, and Inkling AMD's padding (#64690) is covered by this fill.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Clean up sweep workers after the server exits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix benchmark sweep cleanup when a server exits before its workers: terminate the surviving process group and reap the directly owned server process. This update also avoids signalling an already-reaped process group during test cleanup and documents the cleanup scope.

## Claims

- `ServerProcess.stop()` terminates workers remaining in the server's process group after its leader exits.
- Cleanup reaps the direct child and is safe to repeat after successful cleanup.
- The regression's fallback cleanup only signals the group while its direct child has not been reaped.

## Validation

Current candidate is based on main `fce61a05a76ccf34e1af6511ff7071affc306424`. Linux RTX 3090 host, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA devices were hidden throughout these CPU/process tests.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unmodified main plus the same regression tests | 2 failed: direct child unreaped / surviving worker |
| Candidate, standard `tests/benchmarks/sweep` suite with normal conftest fixtures | 28 passed |
| All 17 applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy, markdownlint and test tethering | Passed |
| Diff whitespace check | Passed |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py --timeout=60
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep --timeout=60
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md
```

The tests use real subprocesses, a forked worker, and a socket handshake. The standard suite uses normal global fixtures, with no `--noconftest`. Hooks with no matching files were excluded using their actual file/type filters after an unrelated actionlint environment download failed.

The environment reuses an older official native wheel. No fresh native build, real model-serving or GPU-resource-recovery test, upstream CI, or performance benchmark is claimed. The earlier macOS global-teardown failure remains uninvestigated; this Linux result does not establish that it was fixed.

## Details

`start_new_session=True` makes the server PID the process-group ID. Previously, the `poll() is None` guard prevented cleanup after the leader was reaped, and looking up its PGID required it to remain alive. Signal the known group ID and wait for the direct child; a per-start completion flag prevents repeated successful cleanup from signalling the old group again.

The test's finalizer now checks `returncode` before its emergency signal, addressing the review suggestion about PID/PGID reuse. Closing the worker's socket releases the deliberately orphaned child on failure paths. Production cleanup still covers only workers in the original group, not detached sessions, and does not promise complete GPU-memory recovery. Numeric PGID reuse before the first cleanup remains a limitation.

The rendered benchmark guide at `docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md` describes these semantics. Existing Buildkite benchmark CLI coverage selects the tests. Duplicate-work checks were recorded when the original PR was opened; this updates that same PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex investigated, implemented, and ran the recorded checks.

---

commits.pr_title: [Model] Support data-parallel multimodal encoder for Gemma-4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Enables data-parallel multimodal encoder mode (`--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`) for Gemma-4 by setting `supports_encoder_tp_data = True` on `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` and implementing eager-mode data-parallel ViT execution (`_dp_execute_and_gather`).
- Eliminates redundant replication of the vision encoder across TP ranks in eager mode (`--enforce-eager`).
- Partitions multimodal items across TP ranks using load-balanced assignment, reduces dynamic token lengths across ranks, and scatters gathered embeddings to preserve original sequence order.
---
## 1. Accuracy Verification 
Verified end-to-end against unpartitioned sequential execution across uniform image batches, dynamic mixed aspect ratios, multi-frame video sequences, and empty-rank edge cases:
| Tensor Parallelism | Max Absolute Error | Status |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **TP=1** | **`0.00e+00`** | **PASS (Bitwise exact match)** |
| **TP=2** | **`0.00e+00`** | **PASS (Bitwise exact match)** |
| **TP=4** | **`0.00e+00`** | **PASS (Bitwise exact match)** |
| **TP=8** | **`0.00e+00`** | **PASS (Bitwise exact match)** |
---
## 2. Performance Scaling (TPU v7x-8)
- **Model:** `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic`
- **Hardware:** TPU v7x-8 (GhostFish, 8 cores / 4 chips)
- **Serving Configuration:** `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data --enforce-eager`
- **Workload:** `vllm bench serve` with multimodal input (512×512 images, 512 input tokens, 64 output tokens)

| Tensor Parallelism | Total Throughput (tok/s) | Request Throughput (req/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | TTFT Speedup |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **TP=2** | **472.03 tok/s** | **0.56 req/s** | **39,029.73 ms** | 40,205.52 ms | **1.00x** (Baseline) |
| **TP=4** | **618.72 tok/s** | **0.73 req/s** | **26,081.03 ms** | 26,790.53 ms | **1.50x faster** |
| **TP=8** | **717.08 tok/s** | **0.85 req/s** | **17,705.13 ms** | 18,191.11 ms | **2.20x faster** |

*TP=1 executes via single-rank bypass without collective communication. On TPU, Gemma-4 26B FP8 requires ≥ 2 cores due to the 16 GB HBM limit per core.*

commits.pr_title: [RL][Model Loader] Load plan: plan_loads and TraceTensor
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of #64418 (tracker item P1). Builds on #64336 (direct reload).

Engines that move sharded bytes themselves (sharded RDT, NCCL M2N) need to know, for each
checkpoint tensor, which part this rank needs and where in live memory it goes. This PR adds the
engine-neutral answer from RFC §3/§4:

- `plan_loads(model, metadata)` traces the model's own `load_weights` once, between
  `start_reload` and `finish_reload`, on the tensors direct reload just viewed back;
- it returns a `LoadPlan` with `get_boxes(name)` (what this rank needs) and `get_dest(name)`
  (where it goes); `load_planned` applies it to full tensors.

The NCCL broadcast engine can opt in (`use_load_plan`, off by default), which exercises the plan
end to end. Sharded RDT (E1) and NCCL M2N (E2) move onto it in follow-ups and are the users of
`get_boxes`. Cold start and the existing reload paths are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR implements `plan_loads` or `TraceTensor`. The M0 prototype on #64418
is a measurement tool and is not proposed for merge.

## Assumptions

The plan relies on these and does not check them. A problem that only arises when one is broken
is out of scope here (RFC §1, §5, §6).

**Loaders** (the target models' `load_weights`):
- Each name is handled as it arrives, on its own: no holding a tensor for another name and no
  deferring, within a call or across calls.
- Parameters are written only with `copy_`; a loader never replaces a parameter or buffer.
- State a loader sets is harmless or needed, and nothing that post-load processing or the forward
  reads. The plan runs loaders once and keeps that state.
- No temporaries built with factories on the incoming tensor's device
  (`torch.zeros(..., device=loaded_weight.device)`) and combined with a parameter.

**Updates:**
- Every update sends every name declared at init.
- Post-load processing owns padding and other constants and rewrites them on every update.
- A tensor's storage doesn't move between updates; the address check (aoshen02/vllm#177) will
  catch a move at `finish`.

**Scope:**
- Layerwise reload is being removed (#54477 F7), so changes that break it land with or after F7.
  Sharded RDT moves onto the plan (E1).

## Changes

- **`reload/trace.py`: `TraceTensor`**, a data-free stand-in for an incoming checkpoint tensor.
  View ops return children that know which checkpoint element each of their elements is; a
  dtype-preserving `.to()` is a no-op. A `copy_` from a trace, any other op on it, and value reads
  go to the bake. Modelled on sharded RDT's `FakeRDTTensor`, which is untouched.
- **`reload/bake.py`: the trace.** `load_weights` runs once over traces for all declared names, on
  the model's real tensors as `begin_direct_reload` left them, so the plan and direct reload share
  one layout.
  - A `copy_` from a trace is recorded, not run; it is the only write the plan replays.
  - Any other op on a trace runs on meta copies and makes the name a fallback. A loader that reads
    its destination's values (`param.copy_(fn(param))`, `torch.equal(param, x)`, a mirror copied
    from `param`) also falls back.
  - A value read of a trace (or an op that fails on meta) stops that loader: the name falls back
    and `load_weights` resumes with the names after it.
  - Constant writes into targets run and stay out of the plan (post-load processing owns them).
- **`reload/geometry.py`: pure integer code.** Reduces each `copy_` to a box of the HF tensor and a
  destination region, merges per-expert writes, and computes byte runs for the overlap check.
- **`reload/plan.py`: `plan_loads`, `LoadPlan`, `load_planned`, `check_plannable`.**
  - Refuses layerwise mode, EPLB, planning outside a direct reload, duplicate names, and fallback
    names that write nothing themselves ("move the combine into post-load processing").
  - Names whose writes share a byte become fallbacks and load in arrival order.
  - Names this rank doesn't need get `get_boxes(name) is None` and `get_dest(name) == []`.
  - Logs one line per fallback reason and a summary with the trace time.
  - The required-set check waits for #54477 F2 (`TODO` in `plan_loads`).
- **`reload/direct.py`:** one helper, `direct_reload_active(model)`.

## NCCL engine opt-in

- `use_load_plan` on `NCCLTrainerInitInfo` / `NCCLWeightTransferInitInfo`; with it, `trainer_init`
  also sends the metadata `(name, dtype, shape)`. Out-of-band trainers must send it themselves.
- **Init:** the worker forms the group, then refuses missing metadata, layerwise mode or EPLB,
  destroying the group (the trainer destroys its own too). The model is untouched.
- **First target update:** `start_reload`, then `plan_loads`; the plan is reused for every later
  update. Drafts never plan.
- **Failed plan:** `start_weight_update` raises with a note; later updates use `load_weights`;
  re-init to plan again.
- **Updates:** every trainer rank checks the sent names against the init metadata before any RPC;
  the worker repeats it as a backstop. Received batches go through `load_planned`.
- **Cost:** the trace runs inside the first update. Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16: first sync 7.4 s including
  a 4.2 s trace, against a 2.9 s median for later syncs.

## Known limitations

Beyond the assumptions above:
- **Loaders that skip work when the incoming tensor `is_meta`** leave that write out of the plan.
  In-tree: the DeepGEMM MegaMoE `l2_activation_scale`, which goes stale after a planned update
  (RFC X5). Skips on the *parameter's* `is_meta` now see the real tensor: Kimi-K3's KDA mirrors
  run and their 24 names per rank fall back, correctly.
- **Padding:** padded layers are not expected to be correct on the planned path until #64352 and
  L4 land.
- **Draft models are not planned.**
- **Older servers:** every NCCL init payload now carries `use_load_plan`, so trainer and server
  must be upgraded together.
- **First-update latency:** on a very large model the trace can approach
  `HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient`'s default 300 s timeout; raise `timeout=` there.
- **Reads that bypass the dispatcher** (`tolist()` of a CPU tensor, a raw kernel launch) are not
  seen as destination reads.

## Test Plan

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_load_plan.py` (new, CPU): on small models with real
  vLLM layers under faked TP/EP, planning changes nothing it shouldn't, and two planned reloads
  with new random weights equal a cold start byte for byte at the same addresses. Covers the
  fallback reasons, refusals, resume after a stop, overlaps, fused experts and shared storage.
- `tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py`: the NCCL opt-in (refusals and group teardown on both
  sides, planning at the first update, failed plans, the manifest check, drafts, payloads).
- Weight-sync audit with the state-transition verifier, trace time at scale, and a cold-start A/B.

## Test Result

CPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`) and GPU (GB200, job 45820), nightly wheel 4a0dfc7b2f with this
branch's Python files overlaid:

```
CPU  test_load_plan.py                                     41 passed
CPU  test_weight_transfer.py + test_direct_reload.py       148 passed, 45 skipped, 1 failed
GPU  test_weight_transfer.py                               134 passed, 23 skipped, 1 failed
GPU  test_load_plan.py + test_direct_reload.py
     + test_reload_moe_kernels.py                          80 passed
```

The one failure, `test_sparse_nccl_checkpoint_chunks_to_ep_local_experts_cpu`, is not from this
PR: the sparse engine merged from main imports `refresh_derived_weights`, which the wheel
predates. The GPU jobs ran on 34a61b7895, which differs from the head only in a comment.

### Weight-sync audit

[vllm-state-transition-verifier](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier)
sharded-trainer bench: FSDP=2 trainer → TP2 server on GB200, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, updates
alternating two perturbed checkpoints. `--audit` compares every device tensor (parameters,
buffers, kernel-held) with a fresh server on the last checkpoint.

| Model | Arm | Audit | Mismatched / moved / mem growth | Plan: direct / fallback per rank | First sync | Median sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 | flag off | PASS | 0 / 0 / 0 MiB | — | 2.82 s | 2.83 s |
| | flag on (job 45818) | PASS | 0 / 0 / 0 MiB | 18867 / 0 | 7.37 s (incl. trace) | 2.89 s |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 | flag on (planned at init, 35c34a2907) | PASS | 0 / 0 / 0 MiB | 37248 / 243 | 6.14 s | 5.13 s |
| Kimi-K3-dummy-9L MXFP4 | flag on (job 45819) | 2 mismatched* | 2 / 0 / 0 MiB | 37988 / 24 | 18.9 s (incl. trace) | 7.29 s |

- The FP8 fallbacks are F32 checkpoint tensors (norms, router, embeddings) cast into BF16
  parameters; a trainer that sends BF16 gets them direct.
- \*Both Kimi mismatches are `gemm_rs_ar.partial`, a kernel scratch buffer that also differs
  between two cold starts.
- Sync times come from separate nodes and are not paired (node spread about ±15%).

### Trace time at scale

`plan_loads` per rank, from the checkpoint's own names, dtypes and shapes, right after
`start_reload`, at 15d49bec69 (GB200):

| Model | Parallelism | Names | Trace per rank | Direct / fallback / not needed per rank | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 | TP2 | 18867 | 4.2 s | 18867 / 0 / 0 | 45818 |
| Kimi-K3-dummy-9L MXFP4 | TP2 | 38012 | 9.7–10.2 s | 37988 / 24 / 0 | 45819 |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 FP8 | TP4 + EP4 | 92363 | 16.5–17.6 s | 23671 / 245 / 68447 | 45821 |

- Each name is traced once, so the time grows with the number of names (about 0.18 ms per name).

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] One finish for every update path; drop refresh_derived_weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Every load and weight-update path now finishes through `finalize_model_weights`, and weight-derived state has one hook again: each module's own `process_weights_after_loading()`.

Before this PR the paths finished differently:

| path | quant methods | attention-like layers | other modules' hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold start, direct reload (`process_weights_after_loading`) | yes | yes (loader pass) | yes |
| layerwise reload | yes (per layer) | yes (`_finalize_attention_layer`) | yes |
| sparse NCCL finish | — | **no** | yes |
| kernel-format `reload_weights` | — | **no** | **no** |

#64886 covered the two gaps with a second per-module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, and a walker. Kimi-K3 ROCm's KDA layer is a `MambaBase`, hence attention-like, so `finalize_model_weights` skipped its hook and its decode copies stayed stale after a sparse update or a kernel-format reload.

This PR closes both gaps without a second hook:

- `finalize_model_weights` runs every module's hook in one children-first traversal, attention-like layers included (those under `device_loading_context` when given a target device). Attention hooks need the quant pass done, which the loader does first, and must precede their ancestors' hooks, which children-first gives; no hook reads attention-derived state from a non-ancestor, so there is no separate attention pass. Quant methods and the submodules of quantized layers are still skipped.
- The loader's own attention pass and the hook call in layerwise `_finalize_attention_layer` are removed, so every hook runs once per load, from one place.
- Sparse NCCL ends with `finalize_model_weights` alone.
- Kernel-format `reload_weights` now ends with `finalize_model_weights` too, under `weights_already_processed()`. DeepSeek-V4 ROCm's model hook skips its preshuffle in that mode.
- `refresh_derived_weights` is removed. The Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA and MLA bodies go back into their `process_weights_after_loading()`, which write in place (`copy_`, `refill_derived`).

With every hook guaranteed to run after every load, dummy loads included, these fallbacks are dead and are removed:

- GLM5-next: the wrapper hook that ran its language model's hook a second time (the language model is a submodule, so it already runs), and the indexer's forward-time "post-load processing never ran" call.
- MoE runner: the forward-time build of the fused router + shared-expert gate.
- Qwen3 DFlash and Muse Spark DSpark: the lazy build of the context KV buffers in `precompute_and_store_context_kv`.
- Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark: the lazy build of its context KV metadata.
- Gemma-4 MTP: the forward-time caching of the full lm_head weight (the hook builds it for TP>1).
- Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA: the `is_weights_pre_processed()` early return. The hook only copies `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, which stay in place, so it is valid for pre-processed weights too.

Two hooks are fixed so that they can run on every load:

- Laguna DFlash built its fused context KV inside `load_weights` (per call, and never on dummy loads). It now builds it in `process_weights_after_loading`.
- dots3 vision FP8 MoE returned early after the first run and deleted its checkpoint experts, so a reload had nothing to write. It now keeps the experts and refills the fused buffers in place. Cost: the BF16 vision experts stay resident next to the fused FP8 copy.

Not removed: the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA model hook that calls `specialized_decode` (a plain object, not a module) and the Muse Spark MoE runner calling `post_expert_finalize` (submodules of quantized layers are not walked); both still need their explicit calls.

torchao: inside `reload_weights` the torchao reload decorator is already off. A direct `model.load_weights` reload of a torchao model no longer runs attention hooks. Its removal is proposed in #65913.

Kernel-format weights are not post-processed again, because quant methods do not rerun. As on the sparse path and the weight-cache loader, module and attention hooks must rebuild state from the current weights instead of transforming the weights in place. Direct reload already reruns these same hooks on every update.

Side effect on sparse NCCL: attention hooks now run after a sparse update, so state they derive (for example MLA's `W_UK`/`W_UV` from `kv_b_proj`) is rebuilt as well. Layerwise reload is unchanged apart from where the attention hooks are called from.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), image `vllm-rocm` nightly `3966924d` with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over the installed package, head `8c7b43e05c` (job 33373):

- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`, `test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py`, `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 137 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases of `test_reload_weights`, which fail on the base on this ROCm image too (as in #64886).
- Before the attention change (walker removed, kernel-format reload calling `finalize_model_weights`), `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading[*-float32]` failed: the KDA hook was skipped as an attention-like layer.

NVIDIA A/B, main `831dd92674` vs head `8c7b43e05c` (GSM8K pre vs post, sleep mode, 3 updates, direct and layerwise, throughput before and after):

- No failure is specific to this PR on GLM-5.3-Flash, Nemotron-3.5, Qwen3.5 (fused gate), Qwen3 DFlash, Laguna DFlash, DSv4.1-Flash, Gemma-4 MTP, Muse Spark + DSpark, dots3, Kimi-K3 + DSpark. Throughput is level between arms.
- Fixed by this PR: dots3 direct and layerwise (0.9621→0.9515, 0.9538→0.9545; main fails on `visual.blocks.*.mlp.experts`), Laguna DFlash layerwise (main fails on meta tensors).
- Fail the same on both arms: Kimi-K3 + DSpark direct (illegal memory access after updates), layerwise OOM on Kimi-K3, DSv4.1 and Muse Spark.
- DSv4.1, Gemma-4 and Muse Spark ran with level 1 sleep, because level 2 discards weights the update does not send.

AMD MI350X (gfx950) at `145fb8c684`, sleep level 2 on every update, GSM8K on the first 400 questions:

- Unit tests (job 8289): 140 passed, 2 failed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed. The 2 failures are the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases, which also fail on main.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash AITER=1 (job 8286): direct 0.9700→0.9575, kernel-format 0.9550 / 0.9575 / 0.9550, layerwise 0.9650→0.9575. Throughput 1635→1858 tok/s.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash AITER=0 (job 8287): direct 0.9625→0.9625, kernel-format 0.9650 / 0.9550 / 0.9625. Throughput 823→828 tok/s.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash AITER=1, TP4: direct 0.9000→0.9050 (job 8332), kernel-format 0.8975 / 0.0225 (perturbed) / 0.9025 (job 8357).
- Kimi-K3, truncated checkpoint (jobs 8311, 8288): GSM8K is not meaningful here, so the check is bitwise: derived state is never stale and the KDA copies follow a perturbed update and its restore. Throughput 5720→5922 tok/s.

The kernel-format regression seen at `8c7b43e05c` (DeepSeek-V4 AITER=1, GSM8K 0.0075, double preshuffle) is fixed by `f81b1a7764`.

Same on main, not caused by this PR: DeepSeek-V4 AITER=0 layerwise fails with `too many resources requested for launch`; `_dsv4_wo_a_bf16` is not refreshed (aoshen02/vllm#235).

Open on AMD: DeepSeek-V4.1 layerwise is not attributed (GSM8K 0 with HTTP 400 on main and on `f81b1a7764`, with incomplete runs). One Kimi direct run (job 8288) hung for 30 minutes in an extra update without sleep, with no server error, and did not reproduce in two reruns. DeepSeek-V4 updates ran at TP1 only. Sparse NCCL is covered by unit tests only.

NVIDIA at `145fb8c684`: retest in progress.

Part of RFC #54477.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel] Follow-ups to the gfx942 MLA Triton verify kernel
commits.pr_body:
- Run `test_decode_attention_fwd_verify_int64_page_offset` at 128 heads too, so the 64-row QSPLIT path is checked past 2 GiB, and free cached memory before its free-memory gate.
- `verify_num_kv_splits` takes the launch config from `select_verify_config` itself instead of from the caller.
- Replace `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG` with a private base config that holds only the values both launch configs share.
- Cite ROCm/aiter#6732 in the FP8 V-scale probe and use `_ASM_PADDED_MAX_PS_QLEN` for its qlen bound.
- Fix the `_forward_triton_verify` docstring (only a varlen tail comes back as zeros) and a stale test comment.

These are the non-blocking follow-ups from the review of #62725, plus a few cleanups found by re-reading the merged code. The int64 test used to run only at 16 heads, which always picks the small-tile config, so the QSPLIT path's own page loads were never tested past 2 GiB. With the 128-head case, truncating one QSPLIT page offset to int32 causes an illegal memory access, while the 16-head case still passes. The test's memory gate also counted memory held by the caching allocator as used, so it could skip silently on a busy shard. On the kernel side, `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG`'s `BLOCK_H`, `BLOCK_N`, `num_warps` and `MIN_SPLIT_LEN` were always overridden, and `verify_num_kv_splits` defaulted to a split length the kernel never uses. Having it read the real launch config means the workspace reservation can't drift from the launch. The launch configs and split counts are identical to `main` over 476,280 shapes (batch, qlen, heads, max length and CU count), so there is no perf or accuracy change.

Tests on MI300X: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k verify` passed 10/10 runs (146 passed each, the int64 cases ran rather than skipped), and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` gave 724 passed, 641 skipped, 0 failed.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Frontend] Pin the derender n2 parity cases to top-1 sampling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the `(H200 MIG 35GB) Entrypoints Integration (API Server)` failures on main. Shards 1 and 3 failed in 15 of about 25 main builds on Nov 5, starting with build [100234](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100234). Every failure is the `n2` case of one of two tests in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py`:

- `test_inline_derender_parity[n2]` (line 946):
  ```
  greedy or seeded generation was expected to be deterministic across the coupled and inline calls
  At index 16 diff: 2938 != 88190
  ```
- `test_inline_derender_stream_parity[n2]` (line 1170): the same token comparison, on the streaming path.

**Root cause.** The `n2` case samples at `temperature=0.8` with `seed=42` and asserts that two separate requests (coupled chat vs. inline derender) produce identical token ids. A fixed seed doesn't make sampling reproducible across requests when batching shifts the logits slightly. The two outputs match for 16 tokens and then diverge, which points to numeric drift, not a derender bug. Every greedy case in the same file passes.

The failure rate jumped right after #63231 (default `--block-size` 16 → 64) merged at 09:29 UTC. The last green build was [100208](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100208); the first red one was [100234](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100234), and #63231 is the only change in that window that touches the general KV-cache path. #63231's final head only got a partial `/ci retry` build ([100113](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100113), `kernels-attention-test` only), so this step never ran on it. cc @NickLucche in case the block-size change was meant to keep seeded outputs identical here.

**Fix.** Add `top_k: 1` to both `n2` cases. `n > 1` is rejected for greedy sampling (`temperature=0`), so this keeps the `n=2` multi-choice path while making each step's choice deterministic. Only a genuine near-tie between the top logits could still diverge.

Not a duplicate: there are no open PRs touching this test.

## Test Plan

- Pre-commit passes locally.
- I confirmed the render path carries `top_k` into the generate request via `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py`).
- No GPU locally; this PR's `Entrypoints Integration (API Server)` CI run is the validation.

## Test Result

Pending CI.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63162: honor the tri-state `return_tokens_as_token_ids` override on both disaggregated derender paths, including generate streaming after merged #63103.

## Claims

- Explicit request true/false overrides the answering server's flag; omitted/null falls back to that server's setting.
- `/render` omits the new context key when null, preserving legacy generate compatibility for default requests. Explicit overrides require an upgraded generate node.
- Full and streaming chat/completion logprobs retain their existing placeholder-byte, decoding and hidden-reasoning contracts; raw tokens and non-derender text behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Six new streaming cases with main's serving implementation, keeping the new context field constant | 2 failed / 4 passed before the tokenizer fix; all 6 pass after |
| Incorrect text-only `text_mode` merge negative control | All 6 fail with an error stream |
| Focused protocol, conversion and generation-stream suites, including new cases | 120 passed in 44.77s |
| Full/stream derender routes and render omission cases over HTTP | 34 passed in 82.14s |
| Contributed real-model test using the existing indirect server/client fixtures, Qwen3-0.6B | 2 passed in 102.39s |
| Additional real-model streaming parity probe, both server flags and all request values | 2 passed in 77.93s |
| All applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite tethering | Passed |

The Rust frontend capability check skips the two unsupported render cases. No Rust server E2E, model-quality evaluation or performance benchmark is claimed. Existing entrypoints integration CI selects the changed suites; upstream CI has not run because the contributor pre-run gate remains unsatisfied.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run
```

For the isolated streaming regression, keep the new tests/protocol field and substitute main `3b6eeb0606`'s `serving.py`, then run:

```bash

  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  -k test_stream_derender_logprob_request_override -q
```

```text

2 failed, 4 passed, 60 deselected, 1 warning in 3.49s
```

After restoring the fix:

